tasks.evidence: EXP190 transfers quantize_row_q8_K_ref (CPU Q8_K activation quantization) to Goose. It was chosen by measurement, not by guess: the built libggml-cpu.so contains ZERO ymm/zmm instructions in quantize_row_q8_K, so the executed code is exactly the scalar algorithm, and it is registered at ggml-cpu.c:393 (.from_float) so it is on the --cpu-moe path. Full algorithm in Goose: abs-max scan, zero-block early out, -127/max scale, rounding and clamp, the sixteen group sums and the 1/iscale delta. 8 checks/0 failures, byte-for-byte equality of the whole block_q8_K against quantize_row_q8_K_ref from the real libggml-base.so, sizes 256/512/2560/4096 including an all-zero super-block. Two own defects fixed: the float stride (element j is at byte 4*j, not j, which produced every fourth byte) and nearest_int not being roundf (it adds 12582912.f and masks the mantissa: round-half-to-even, unlike roundf). APEX EXECUTION CHECK: NEGATIVE. An LD_PRELOAD shim overriding quantize_row_q8_K_ref was validated standalone (2 calls to Goose, 0 native, byte-identical) and then loaded into a real Apex run: output exact but no witness, and objdump finds no call site to quantize_row_q8_K in libggml-cpu at all. The CPU MoE graph reaches the expert matmul (op=100,42560 calls) and dense matmul (op=40,138 calls) directly, both already covered by EXP143. So the module is byte-exact but off the Apex path, like EXP182 and EXP188. No performance claim. The portable-ISA scope is NOT closed: ggml_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_K has 58 SIMD instructions and ggml_vec_dot_q6_K_q8_K has 91 on this host, Goose has no SIMD, and the compiler documentation places SIMD outside current scope, so the quantized dot families remain native. DUPLICATE FOUND 2026-11-08: EXP190 transferred quantize_row_q8_K_ref, but the Apex log already carries FG148_QUANT kind=9 calls=456800 values=172640 -- EXP148 installed a Goose Q8_K encoder into the CPU type-trait table (source/quant/unit.c:43, kind=9 width 256 stride 292), so the native function this module replaces is unreachable on the executed path. A loaded LD_PRELOAD probe confirmed the negative directly: its wrapper never fired in a real Apex run while the same probe worked in a standalone DSO test. EXP190 is therefore a duplicate of completed work, not remaining scope, and is marked DUPLICATE. Same lesson as EXP188: read the executed implementation, not the first match by name, and check the type-trait table before porting a from_float. 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P1-11-INVENTORY.md). Backends: only base, cpu and cuda libraries exist in build-cuda/bin -- no Metal/Vulkan/SYCL/OpenCL/ROCm, recorded as hardware-unavailable rather than missing; CPU has Goose core/buffers/streams/allocator (EXP160-163) plus the CPU backend module (EXP143, FG143 counters live), CUDA has Goose device modules (FG183F/FG171R/FG167/FG169T live) over native driver primitives. Base: flint's nine objects map one-for-one -- ggml.c+ggml.cpp -> base-ggmlcpp.o+shared-core.o (Goose core EXP160), ggml-backend.cpp -> backend-scheduler.o+scheduler-goose.o (EXP164) with backend-base-goose.o keeping native symbols, ggml-alloc.c -> allocator.o (EXP161), ggml-backend-meta.cpp -> shared-meta.o (EXP160), while ggml-quants.c, ggml-opt.cpp, ggml-threading.cpp and gguf.cpp stay native (gguf deliberately, P7-01); buffers-goose.o and stream-goose.o are new Goose layers (EXP162/163). Remaining: one row per CPU object and per CUDA family saying Goose-dispatched vs audited primitive. 2026-11-12 CLOSED. tasks.evidence: 2026-11-15 decision note (docs/goose-migration/P1-12-DECISION.md): the CPU MoE orchestration is Goose (ar_ recipe matching, xl_ LRU/residency/budget, dw_ dense placement, sp_ row-stream plan, rh_/ov_/rs_ router hooks and overlap, meta backend and optimizer). The dot-product kernels themselves are SIMD and cannot move: Goose has no intrinsic surface, so they are substrate in the same category as libc/libm. Closing the criterion needs Igor's decision: (A) reclassify SIMD as substrate and close, (B) keep it open until a Goose vector surface exists, (C) close only the orchestration part. Recommendation: B, unless Igor states that SIMD is substrate project-wide. 2026-11-15 EXP665 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-665-p1-12-simd-delivery): the compiler owner's SIMD delivery 8b7a56bb (commit 7738b34a) is VERIFIED from the runtime side. Both published hashes match (compiler 8b7a56bb..., blocks.o 67f7f760...). The author's verifier reproduces 16384 blocks per arm, integer exact, float bit-exact on five arms. A second, independent oracle in integration/p1-12/tests links blocks.o against the unmodified native sources ggml-quants.c, ggml-cpu/quants.c and ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c: 16384 comparisons, 0 failures, integer minima and fp32 bit-identical including signed zero, and 0 spread against the native AVX2 kernels. Four single-block entry points q4_K x q8_K, q6_K x q8_K, q8_0 x q8_0, q4_0 x q8_0 on AVX2+FMA with scalar fallback. Not covered: NEON/SVE/AVX512/VNNI, multi-thread application support, performance. The substrate blocker is gone; integration into the CPU MoE switch is the remaining work. 2026-11-15 EXP667 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-667-p1-12-switch): the switch landed. integration/p1-12/src/fg-goose-cpu-simd.cpp routes the four single-block dots to the delivered kernels behind FG_GOOSE_CPU_SIMD_NATIVE (rule 10: unset means Goose). Differential gate against ggml_vec_dot_*_generic: 4096 routed calls at 1024 iterations, 0 failures, bit-identical fp32; the native arm of the same binary reports goose_calls=0; a multi-block row (nb=4) is refused so a one-block kernel can never silently drop a tail. The bridge references the delivered object weakly, so a build without it stays native. 2026-11-15 EXP668 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-668-p1-12-multiblock-limit): the multi-block boundary is measured, not assumed. Summing single-block results differs from the native row kernel in 59/128 (nb=2), 62/128 (nb=4) and 56/128 (nb=8) cases, up to 3 ULP (2.67e-07), while nb=1 is exact. Cause is structural: the native row kernel keeps one __m256 accumulator across all blocks and folds it once at the end, so a sum of already-horizontal-reduced scalars has a different association. A row-level entry point was requested from the compiler owner (mailbox runtime-row-contract-p1-12-20261115T1315Z). Until it exists the row loop stays native, which is the recorded P1-12 boundary. 2026-11-18 EXP-2026-11-18-1007: the row-level delivery was checked against the live runtime instead of a bench build. The chain is fg143_try (declines every quantized MUL_MAT_ID: entry.goose:42-45 and matrix.goose:65-77) -> fg140_dispatch -> fg140_previous_mul_mat_id -> CPU_REPACK for Q4_K (supports_op true for a 3-D Q4_K expert tensor; FG404 is the native first-supported rule) -> ggml_gemv_q4_K_8x8_q8_K. The delivered row object is bit-exact with ggml_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_K (256/256) and differs from the live gemv in 188/207/227 of 256 cases at n=512/2048/8192, up to 2.624e-04 relative and 3584 ULP; the generic order matches neither. EXP411's runtime detour already measured zero calls to every quantized vec_dot on the accepted profile. P1-12's Q4_K part was therefore BLOCKED on a missing numerical contract and ABI, not on a compiler capability. No production change, no model run. 2026-11-18 EXP-2026-11-18-1008: the missing entry was implemented in Goose (src/moe_gemv.goose, exact lane-for-lane transcription of the AVX2 body, built with qualified compiler 8b7a56bb and gcc-13 -O3 -mavx2 -mfma) and proves bit-identical to the live kernel on 28800/28800 cases across n=512/2048/8192 and nc=8/16/64/512. The numerical contract is closed. The remaining blocker is generated-code performance: --packed reports maddubs NONE and the lane shuffles are emitted as scalar loops, so the object runs 271x slower than native (23.9 us vs 6531.2 us at n=2048 nc=512) and the accepted EXP665 row object measures 383-576x slower than vec_dot. At 1.03 GMAC/token this projects to roughly 0.8 s/token against the accepted ~40 tok/s, so wiring it in would be a confirmed decode regression; A/B, C++ removal and DONE are not reached. No production file, reference binary or model was touched. 2026-11-18 IRONBEAK: the compiler owner delivered Fried Goose v0.1.3-preview (releases/experimental/p112-ironbeak-preview, binary sha256 241e3fa4..., commit 64afce6a; sha256sum -c OK; stdlib byte-identical to the copy in the experiment). Rebuilt per the handoff into experiments/EXP-2026-11-18-1008-p1-12-gemv/build/p112: emit+compile rc 0, 64 AVX2 instructions in the object, gate_x8 28800/28800 equal with max ulp 0, bench_x8 2048 512 2000 native 24.1 us vs Goose 44.5 us = 1.84x, diffs 0. The 271x blocker is therefore reduced to 1.84x; the scalar baseline object is preserved as build/libmoe_gemv.baseline.so (sha256 68ceb389...). An A/B hook (src/gemv_preload.c -> build/libironbeak_hook.so) patches the loaded ggml_gemv_q4_K_8x8_q8_K entry and is validated without a model: with FG_IRONBEAK_HOOK=0 the native arm is 22.9 us, with the hook 47.8 us and 0 diffs, witness IRONBEAK_HOOK first_call n=2048 nc=512 nr=1. tasks.evidence: All four located defects closed and verified on 2026-11-12. SILU: the standalone op now uses the AVX2-compatible association (cause was unary_value always calling scalar silu; 247/1000 values diverged across the vectorised head, not the tail). clamp: the native MIN/MAX macros return the second operand on an unordered comparison, unlike fminf/fmaxf -- traced at run time, fminf(0x7f800001,0.5) returns the quieted NaN 0x7fc00001 and the composed bound became -0.5 where native gives +0.5; clamp now uses native_min/native_max helpers that reproduce the macro form. scale: a zero bias is skipped so -0 keeps its sign. Probe tools/p2-01-contract with the rebuilt libggml-cpu: 40 cases, 36 bit-identical, including both quiet-NaN payloads, the signalling NaN, signed zero, subnormals, threads 1/8 and four strided cases (SILU, CLAMP, ADD on a row-strided 2-D view; SCALE cannot be probed strided because native asserts full contiguity). Remaining expected divergences are norm_finite, softmax_finite, mul_mat_32x8x6, rope_16x2x4 -- other items, ULP-close. Apex 32K/128 with the rebuilt library: e68df05b, probabilities equal, restore exact, slot 387989920 bytes. Build notes: the pinned v61 compiler rejects codec/decode.goose:125 (i64->i32 narrowing), so the module was regenerated with the artifact compiler stage3-454151b3449b; the bridge is unaffected because it calls only gg_function_1, whose signature is unchanged. Remaining gap for closure: the probe covers F32 only; other element types for binary/unary/GLU are not exercised. CLOSED 2026-11-12: non-F32 coverage added. The probe now runs F16 and BF16 for the supported combinations (native scale handles F32/BF16, clamp handles F32/F16 -- the other pairings abort in the native forward and are recorded as non-contracts). One real defect found by the new cases: scale_bf16 on -0 gave 8000 against native 0000, because the F32 forward skips a zero bias while the BF16 forward always computes s*x+b; the port now follows the asymmetry per destination type. Gap: K-quants (Q2_K..Q6_K), I-quants (IQ2_XXS/ XS/ S, IQ3_XXS/ S, IQ1_S/ M, IQ4_NL/ XS), MXFP4, TQ1_0/2_0 and the repack variants. Each needs the EXP148 treatment (encoder/decoder, byte-exact gate over several sizes with a degenerate block, and a live witness) preceded by the EXP190 check: read the executed symbol and confirm it is scalar before porting, because a SIMD body falls under the recorded compiler-scope exclusion. 2026-11-12 FIRST PORT (EXP-310): Q4_K decode in Goose, byte-exact against dequantize_row_q4_K from libggml-base over sizes 256/512/2560/4096 with a degenerate zeroed super-block: EXP310_Q4K checks=7424 failures=0. The whole algorithm is Goose (d/dmin read, get_scale_min_k4 both branches, four 64-output groups, low then high nibbles, d1*q-m1); externs are byte load, half-to-float and float store only. Mutation (scale +1 for the second group) produced 3025 of 7424 divergences, so the gate is sensitive. Not yet wired into the type-trait table, so no live witness and none claimed. Next: wire it, then port Q6_K, the other type the Q4_K_M model uses. 2026-11-12 SECOND PORT (EXP-311): Q6_K decode in Goose, EXP311_Q6K checks=7424 failures=0 against dequantize_row_q6_K over 256/512/2560/4096 with a degenerate super-block; mutation (scale +1) gave 1717 divergences, reverted to green. LAYOUT LESSON: this fork orders block_q6_K as ql[128], qh[64], scales[16], d at offsets 0/128/192/208 (verified with offsetof); the upstream order puts d first and the first attempt using it failed 7329 of 7424. block_q4_K does match the familiar order (d 0, dmin 2, scales 4, qs 16, size 144), so EXP310 needed no correction. Live: neither decoder is wired into the type-trait table yet; a preload probe on dequantize_row_q4_K saw zero calls, but libggml-base is linked -Bsymbolic so the probe is blind to internal calls and the result proves nothing either way. 2026-11-12 THIRD PORT (EXP-312): Q5_K decode in Goose, EXP312_Q5K checks=7424 failures=0 against dequantize_row_q5_K over 256/512/2560/4096 with a degenerate super-block; layout pinned with offsetof (176 bytes: d 0, dmin 2, scales 12 at 4, qh 32 at 16, qs 128 at 48); mutation (mask shift by 1 instead of 2) gave 1202 divergences, reverted to green. WIRING DEFERRED deliberately: installing the decoders in the type-trait table requires rebuilding/relinking libggml-base, the exact library under the P6-02 blocker whose deployed bytes cannot be reproduced; doing it now would replace the artifact the Apex baseline is measured against and muddy that diagnosis. 2026-11-12 FOURTH PORT (EXP-313): Q2_K decode in Goose, EXP313_Q2K checks=7424 failures=0 against dequantize_row_q2_K over 256/512/2560/4096 with a degenerate super-block; layout pinned with offsetof (84 bytes: scales 0, qs 16, d 80, dmin 82); mutation (shift += 3) gave 2926 divergences, reverted to green. Own-fixture defect found and fixed: the inherited degenerate-block memset used a hardcoded 144 bytes, which overflowed Q2_K's 84-byte blocks (fortify aborted the run) and only partially zeroed EXP311's 210-byte blocks; EXP311 now zeroes the full block and still reports 7424/0. 2026-11-12 K FAMILY COMPLETE (EXP-314): Q3_K decode in Goose, EXP314_Q3K checks=7424 failures=0 against dequantize_row_q3_K over 256/512/2560/4096 with a degenerate block; layout pinned with offsetof (110 bytes: hmask 0, qs 32, scales 96, d 108); the 6-bit scales are unpacked with the reference's four word shuffles and the high-bit mask m shifts once per 16-element run without reset between halves; mutation (m <<= 2) gave 2620 divergences, reverted to green. tasks.notes: MMQ Q8_1 feeder ported byte-exact (EXP180) but NOT promoted. SASS: Goose kernel<0>=400, <1>=355 against native DS4 157 direct / 227 scatter, measured with cuobjdump -sass -fun per mangled name (earlier 824-vs-160 and 432/392/168/264 came from looser extraction and are withdrawn; the 2.55x/1.56x ratio was stable). ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED IN A VARIANT (EXP222): the 2.6x was almost entirely a DEAD branch. The source guards two int64 divisions behind `if ne2i == 1`, ne2 is a runtime kernel argument (ds and scatter are pinned as wrapper constants, ne2 is not), so the divisions survived in every instantiation while every Apex call has ne2 == 1. Pinning it: 400 -> 164 instructions (native 157, near parity), IMAD.HI.U32 22 -> 0, and goose time 2078.8 -> 2002.0 ns mean (-3.69%), gap against native 13.79% -> 11.31%. Byte-exact: fixture checks=8 failures=0 both arms, output dumps files=4 differing=0. Variant source is experiments/EXP-2026-11-10-222-mmq-ne2-specialization/. NOT PROMOTED: 11.31% > 2% rule, and the variant is valid only for ne2 == 1 while the fixture never exercises ne2 != 1. REMAINING GAP LOCATED: scatter kernel 355 vs 227. Opcode diff shows BPT.TRAP 6 vs 0 -- the six ensure() guards inlined as traps, with ISETP.GT.AND.EX / UIADD3 / UFLO.U32 / UMOV around them: about 30 of the 128 instructions are validation the port adds and native omits. Rest is 64-bit constant materialisation (IMAD.MOV.U32 +22, UMOV +11, IADD3.X +10, IMAD.U32 +19). NEXT, IN ORDER: (1) gate ensure() behind a compile-time debug flag for the Apex build, measure; (2) only if a gap above 2% remains, attack 64-bit constant materialisation. Promotable shape for ne2: a fifth wrapper constant selecting between two Goose bodies. Known obstacle recorded before starting: emit_sources.py asserts exactly 2 entries are called from main and the CUDA host maps wrappers by emitted function index, so adding wrappers means re-deriving those #defines from the new emission. Profiling is unavailable here: ncu returns ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, nsys aborts the server under tracing (profiling-unavailable-2026-11-10.md). || WITHDRAWN: EXP224/225/226 claimed Apex A/B results; the runner strips all GGML_GOOSE_* variables and applies a frozen EXP150 snapshot, so both arms were the same configuration and every delta is noise (docs/goose-migration/measurement-env-stripped.md). The MMQ Apex question is OPEN, not answered. || EARLIER TEXT (void): measured at Apex on the CURRENT lineage for the first time. The route is already inside the shipped DSO behind GGML_GOOSE_CUDA_MMQ_Q8_1, so no rebuild was needed. EXP224 (in-chain typed variant): pairs -2.62% / +3.38% decode, mean +0.37%. EXP225 (chain DSO rebuilt from EXP208's own link line with the MMQ object replaced by u64+ne2, both arms same DSO): pairs -4.56% / +2.12%, mean -1.23%. Tokens and all 128 probabilities exact in every run. MEANS ARE INSIDE 2% BUT THE VARIANT QUESTION IS NOT RESOLVED: pairs swing 6.7 points, and the two variants' means differ by 1.6 points, four times smaller than the spread that produced them. Do not rank them from Apex data. Decide the variant on EXP208's kernel-level evidence (u64 1848.8/1831.9 ns vs typed 1922.6/1958.4 ns, byte-exact both), which used one harness with tight spread. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS ALSO FOUND: (a) the chain links EXP208's TYPED variant, which EXP208 itself rejected as 4-6.5% slower than its u64 source -- the recorded link line names runtime/exp208/build/cuda-mmq-q8-1.o; (b) the switch is strcmp(flag,"1")==0, opt-in, against rule 10, and the EXP180 fixture mislabels the unset case as arm=goose while the dispatcher runs native. Neither is fixed yet. || EXP235 (this session): the Q4_K inner product vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_impl_mmq is ported, BIT-EXACT on GPU (65536 elements, worst_rel=0) and AT PARITY at kernel level (native 173.8 ns vs goose 174.2 ns, +0.29%, six interleaved runs) -- but ONLY after declaring dp4a as an extern primitive. With the byte products written out longhand the emission produced 741 instructions vs native's 133, no IDP.4A at all, and +19.2% time. The primitive route is mine to take and needs nothing from the compiler; the defect report I filed was withdrawn. The surrounding TILE loop (ggml_cuda_mmq_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_dp4a) is also ported and verified equal (512 cases, 0 differences) but is 2.1x SLOWER (3432.6 vs 7233.9 ns/tile) and stays unwired. Two redesigns; the residual is structural: (a) the accumulator cannot stay in a register because the module receives it as a base pointer, (b) geometry arrives as i64 arguments instead of constexpr, (c) the emission emits a while loop where native has #pragma unroll over 2xJxI. MEASURED RULE for hot-loop ports: an inner function whose whole state can be named as primitives ports at parity; a loop that owns an accumulator and constant geometry does not, until the language can express 'keep this in a register across the loop' and 'this bound is a constant'. || EXP236 + MMA ANALYSIS (decisive): on sm_89 the Q4_K/Q6_K inner products are NOT on the live path. common.cuh:289 defines TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE when __CUDA_ARCH__ >= TURING, and ggml_cuda_mmq_get_util_funcs only reaches the dp4a branch when use_mma_data_layout() is false. On this GPU it is always true, so mul_mat_q uses IMMA.16816.S8.S8 (512 of them in the Q6_K kernel) and vec_dot_*_impl_mmq is never called. Verified: all 32 mul_mat_q kernels are instruction-identical to stock when the dp4a body is patched. So the census's 40% is MMA code, and MMA is NOT expressible in this module format: it is warp-collective tensor-core programming (lane-indexed fragments, ldmatrix, mma.sync, three #elif variants with different strides). A module receives a base pointer and scalars; it has no notion of a per-lane value or a matrix-fragment-typed shape. Opaque primitives for ldmatrix/mma would leave the lane bookkeeping outside, which is a rename, not a port. FORCED-dp4a PROBE (copied tree, GGML_FORCE_DP4A_PROBE): the dp4a path is instantiated, 28672 IDP.4A appear, the Goose port BINDS, and the Q6_K kernel is 4047 instructions vs native's 4079 -- 32 FEWER, with an identical opcode histogram, so the difference is scheduling not algorithm. First configuration in this line where Goose is not larger. Not a promotion: forcing dp4a disables tensor cores for EVERY K-quantised type. WIRING MECHANISM SOLVED: neither -I nor -D nor -include works (a quoted include resolves in the includer's directory first; -D renames the call sites too). Copying the whole ggml-cuda directory and compiling from inside the copy works -- byte-identical cubins had hidden three failures.

tasks.evidence: EXP191 runs the THIRTEEN modules that have a standalone GPU fixture (174,175,176,177,178,179,180,181,182,183,184,185,188) under compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and initcheck from one script with a machine-readable artifact. FINAL RESULT: all thirteen are clean under all three tools, zero exceptions. An earlier version reported 5 racecheck hazards in EXP181 and excused them as inherent because the native arm showed 18; that reasoning was wrong. The hazards came from the FIXTURE generating duplicate experts within one token, which a router never emits: compaction writes the packed (token,expert) slot at it_compact+inclusive_prefix, so a duplicated expert makes two lanes of one 8-wide group target the same staging address. With a distinct expert set per token both arms report zero hazards (native 18->0, Goose 5->0), the kernel was never racy, and the exemption was deleted from the script so any non-zero result now fails. Lesson recorded: a comparison showing native is worse does not prove the difference is inherent, it can mean both are fed input the operator does not accept. Limit: per-module fixtures, not the CUDA DSO as a whole, because a whole-library sanitizer run does not fit next to a 35B model in 11.8GB. 2026-11-12 FULL-MATRIX MILESTONE (EXP365), closing the three gaps EXP191 left. (1) synccheck is now run: the criterion names four tools, EXP191 ran three. (2) the module list is DISCOVERED from runtime/exp*/build/gpu-fixture instead of hand-written, so the 28 fixtures added after EXP191 cannot be skipped silently: 41 modules x 4 tools = 164 runs, every one zero. (3) every fixture must pass on its own with zero failures before it is sanitized, because a sanitizer finding on a failing fixture is a statement about the fixture. TWO DEFECTS FOUND, BOTH IN FIXTURES, NOT IN MODULES: the first run reported 689 memcheck errors on EXP281 and 693 on EXP282, all inside soft_max_f32_ref<true,0,0,half> -- the NATIVE reference kernel -- reading past a 2400-byte allocation. Cause: native takes mask strides from the mask tensor (softmax.cu:413-415), so a half mask has half the strides, but both fixtures set nb11=4*ncols once and reused it for the F16 arm, handing the same strides to a mask allocated at 2*ncols per row; both the native kernel and the Goose module then read past the mask, which is why a plain run compared two out-of-bounds reads as byte-identical. Fix: nb11=2*ncols (and dependent strides) before the F16 launch, matching the native launcher; rebuilt as gpu-fixture-fixed for both. After: EXP281 and EXP282 plain 0 failures, memcheck 0. The two corrected fixtures and their patch are kept under experiments/EXP-2026-11-12-365-sanitizer-milestone-full/fixtures/, and the runner prefers a gpu-fixture-fixed binary when present so the correction cannot be silently ignored. grep dmsh shows only these two fixtures hand a mask to a half arm, so the defect does not extend further. EXP310 adds kpool_pad, kpool_rank and the per-sequence layout update: resume from the scan point when clean and the first position matches, rebuild when stale or shrinking, and both grouping modes (by order and by position with alignment plus consecutive positions); 32 147 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP311 adds the state ordering: the indexer suffix on write, the mirrored restore order with the layout hand-over, the failure transaction dropping the sequence from all three caches, state_drop clearing directly, and the ubatch stream count; 22 290 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP312 adds kpool_build_state: generation-stamped marks, the stale pass (pools ending after an edited position), the token pass in both modes, representative-row uniqueness and the graph-size bound; 23 587 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP313 adds the context stepping: next clears staleness marks only on the first step, apply ANDs both sides and only then extends the layout and pins the pool step, and kpool_track is derived; 19 405 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP315 adds the base hybrid memory policy: per-cache external filters with the recurrent pattern as the default, the batch split choice (by sequence for all-output batches, else equal with the non-sequential form and the rollback window inside one ubatch), the prepare order with the recurrent cache first, and the attention stream count; 23 582 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP314 adds set_input_kpool: the pool tables (representative row, member cells, sentinel for absent sequences, distinct padding cells, M-RoPE positions) and the masks (visible prefix by rank or position, selection slots, tail cells); 212 205 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. tasks.evidence: EXP321 transfers the cell selection of llama_kv_cache::state_write: a cell is written when it is non-empty, carries the requested sequence (all cells when the sequence is -1), and is not excluded by the sliding window at the sequence's highest position; consecutive cells are coalesced into ranges whose lengths must equal the per-stream counts, and the partial-only flag drops the section for a cache without a window. Gate: 40 670 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP322 adds state_write_meta: per cell the position, id count, extension when present and the ids in increasing order, with a named sequence writing only itself and an unnamed write carrying all; 109 429 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP323 adds the state_write_data plan: header (layout flag, layer count, both rotation sizes), per-layer key type/row size with one transfer per range, the plain-V repetition, and the transposed-V walk with the embedding dimension outermost; 65 202 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP324 adds state_read_meta in both branches with six rejection codes: single-sequence (fit check, destination removal, exact one-id records, mirrored layout or search, extension restored after the batch) and whole-cache (cells from zero, count-only mirror check, id range check, head reset); 6 715 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations caught. EXP325 closes state_read_data: contiguous-run batching of destination indices, header validation order and codes, and record order (layer outermost, then embedding row for transposed V, then runs); 50 384 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. P5-08 write/read pair is now covered end to end at plan level. EXP344 adds state_read_sinfo orchestration and both state_clear overloads: mirrored and partial-only exits, layout/stream guards before I/O, one up-front clear, empty mirrored layout per zero-cell stream, clear-before-throw, cell collection limited to singly-held cells, and the contiguous/per-cell clear body. 42 287 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations. EXP345 adds state_write range collection: non-empty cells holding the sequence, SWA-masked only for a real sequence (never for -1), contiguous coalescing, and zero-cell streams skipped without meta or data. 39 388 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations covering all four masking types. 2026-11-12 interop probe (EXP-292): native->goose restore continues deterministically (content 1da0f499 equals the original native answer, n_restored=12); goose->native restore reports n_restored=12 but the continuation differs (0b7d5391). Files: native 131975288 bytes, goose 131976068 (+780); headers identical, first differences from byte 605 inside per-cell metadata. So our reader is compatible, our writer is not -- the native reader accepts the file but reconstructs a different KV. Remaining: align state_write cell selection/order with native and explain the +780 bytes. Truncation/error paths are covered (EXP363/364, EXP366). 2026-11-12 narrowing: the size delta is essentially constant, not per-cell -- a 2-token prompt gives +792 (65946744 vs 65947536), the 12-token prompt +780 (131975288 vs 131976068) -- so it is a fixed section, not cell ordering. Blanket bisect is unavailable: with all 61 GGML_GOOSE_* switches at 0 the server does not start; the four KV switches alone left the file byte-identical. Next: parse both files' state_write_data headers with the writer's own layout to name the extra section. 2026-11-12 third probe: the earliest difference between the two writers' files is numeric -- offset 480, native 0xC0003574 vs goose 0xC0003575, one ULP in a KV value -- while the header (magic, seq id, stream counts) matches and the following bytes continue identically. So the native reader does parse our file; its continuation flips because of one-ULP KV sensitivity at temperature 0, which is a property of the two compute lines, not of the serialization. The fixed +780 bytes remain open and are a separate layout question (data-section header or padding), to be named from the writer layout. 2026-11-12 fourth probe: a parser built from the writers' layout walks both files end to end under the same field sequence (each lands 4 bytes short of its own size -- a common trailer), so the format is structurally identical; the earlier 'fixed section' hypothesis is corrected -- the delta is counted content. The transposed-V branch is not taken by this corpus. Which counted value differs is not yet named; reverse engineering is the wrong tool, so the next step is instrumenting io.n_bytes() after meta and after each layer in a patched writer and diffing the section sizes between lines. 2026-11-12 fifth probe: the slot file has its own framing before the state blob -- magic 0x67677371, seq/version 4, 16, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, n_tokens=12 at offset 20, then the 12 prompt token ids from 24 -- identical in both lines. The earlier 'walk to EOF-4' claim is withdrawn as a wrong layout that landed near the end. The 1-ULP KV difference sits at absolute offset 480 in BOTH files, so the state region starts at the same place and stays aligned past the first K rows; the +780 must arise further down (later layers or the V section). Next: finish mapping the state offset (offset 72 still shows a token-like value) and compare per-layer boundaries. 2026-11-12 FOUND: the +780 bytes are one extra checkpoint. Both files carry the SCKP appendix at the same offset 66110808 (main state same size); native has count=1 [n_tokens=5, pos 4..4, 65864428 B], ours has count=2 with an extra first entry [n_tokens=0, pos 0..-1, 740 B] whose bytes are 8+8+24+740 = 780 exactly. The second entry is byte-identical to native's. So the format is not at fault: our server creates an empty checkpoint at zero tokens (create_checkpoint reached with n_tokens_cur == prompt.n_tokens()), a server-side trigger question, likely the batch split or the checkpoint policy (EXP268). Remaining for closure: remove the empty checkpoint, and state the one-ULP KV sensitivity between compute lines explicitly. 2026-11-12 ROOT CAUSE of the empty checkpoint: the incremental seq-position bounds from EXP209 live in a process-wide arena (static inline int64_t* goose_bounds, llama-kv-cells.h:49) because a member would change sizeof(llama_kv_cells) for the unchanged flint objects. seq_pos_min returns goose_bounds[seq_id] directly, so every cache instance shares the same slots, and reset() clears the cells but not the arena. A freshly reset slot therefore reports 0 instead of -1, the 'nothing to checkpoint yet' guard passes, and an empty checkpoint is written (+780 bytes). Fix: per-instance arena keyed by the cells object, zeroed in reset(); the class layout cannot change while flint objects link against the old sizeof. 2026-11-12 FIXED AND CLOSED (EXP-293). Cause: the EXP209 incremental sequence bounds lived in one process-wide arena and reset() never cleared it, so a reset slot reported seq_pos_min=0 instead of -1 and an empty checkpoint was written (+780 B). Fix: per-instance arena keyed by this (8-slot table, native fallback when exhausted) plus clearing on reset, with the class layout untouched because the variant caches are flint objects compiled against the stock header; three TUs recompiled and substituted. Verified: checkpoint appendix count=1, state file size 131975288 == native's, Apex e68df05b with 128 tokens, native->goose restore exact (1da0f499), goose->native restore parses with n_restored=12. Documented boundary: the two compute lines differ by one ULP in KV values (offset 480), which at temperature 0 can flip a token in the goose->native direction -- a property of the kernels, not of the serialization. Truncation and header errors remain covered (EXP363/364/366/367/368).

tasks.title: Port model object and tensor binding lifecycle
tasks.acceptance: All model tensor ownership,backend attachment,metadata queries and unload/error cleanup implemented with ABI parity.
tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P6-02-INVENTORY.md). State: llama-model.cpp has no Goose hooks at all; its only differences from flint are the expert-pin include block and pin owner/mutex members (96 added, 0 removed). Surface size: 94 buft/buffer_type references, 39 ggml_backend_buffer references with 5 allocation sites, 5 metadata entry points, and the destructor/free/pin-ordering cleanup. Slices in order: (1) unload and error cleanup -- smallest, most bug-prone, testable with a failing load and the existing unload path; (2) tensor ownership and backend attachment -- the real work, extending the already-live loader decisions EXP403/EXP404 (FG404S_WEIGHT_PLACEMENT); (3) metadata queries -- pure but ABI-sensitive (snprintf would-be length, -1 with buf[0]=0, unordered index order), most likely to close as a stated native boundary. Done means each area has a module or a recorded boundary with a reason, a gate that fails under mutation, and a live witness or an explicit dormancy statement. 2026-11-12 CLOSED (EXP-303). Backend attachment is ported and live: llama-model-loader.cpp:1122-1138 asks fg404s_decide for both the no-op first-buffer case and the per-device probe loop, with weight_buft_supported as the native predicate; FG404S_WEIGHT_PLACEMENT appears in the accepted run. Tensor ownership is native by design (alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft, no_alloc dummy buffer, host-pointer mapping, mlock) and exercised by the full 40-block load. Metadata parity measured with a direct C-API probe on both lines: 47 entries, identical FNV hash d4e54caca421a3c8 over every key/value in index order, miss -1 with buf[0]=0, truncation returns 9 with 'qwe', buf_size 0 returns 9. Cleanup parity measured: load+free exits 0 on both lines, the three invalid-GGUF fixtures give identical messages and exit 1, and the expert-pin owner is released before buffers and mmaps with buffers held by ggml_backend_buffer_ptr. Boundary: ownership, cleanup and string formatting stay native -- the categories the migration rule keeps native -- and are recorded with measured parity; the one area with a real decision is ported and live. 2026-11-12 REOPENED (EXP-304): a second prompt shape contradicts the closure. With -ngl 0 and no CUDA device line in either log, the 371-token prompt aborts on our line while native answers (c5ca940bbe49eaa5): ggml_backend_tensor_copy -> fg163_io -> ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor raises 'CUDA error: invalid argument' (shared-cuda.cu:114). The log shows a recurrent prefix checkpoint written at tokens=1 just before. A copy driven by fg163 reaching a CUDA buffer under -ngl 0 is an ownership/attachment defect, so P6-02 stays IN_PROGRESS until it is explained and fixed; re-closing requires both the 5-token and 371-token shapes green. 2026-11-12 LOCALIZED (EXP-304 continued): a breakpoint on ggml_backend_tensor_copy stops inside the scheduler -- fg164_component <- fg164_gg_function_84 <- fg164_gg_function_1 <- ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async <- llama_context::graph_compute <- process_ubatch. The copy is part of graph scheduling for the 371-token ubatch and its destination is a CUDA buffer despite -ngl 0 and no CUDA device line; the short prompt never reaches this split. So the defect is the scheduler's backend assignment for a split graph (EXP164), not weight placement and not the recurrent checkpoint. Next: read what fg164 returns for that node and whether the index is in range. 2026-11-12 ISOLATED (EXP-304): the same reproducer with our libllama and the flint libggml-base answers the long prompt with zero CUDA errors, while our libggml-base aborts. So the fault is the scheduler replacement in our base library. All switches (GGML_GOOSE_SCHEDULER=0, GGML_GOOSE_CPU_BACKEND_API=0) still abort, so it is not a hook. ggml_backend_tensor_copy and ggml_backend_sched_backend_id_from_cur are textually identical to flint's; the replacement is a different revision (expert_pipeline appears 16 times in ours, 0 in the flint ggml-backend.cpp), so its behaviour cannot be assumed preserved. Under -ngl 0 the CUDA split should not exist. Next: compare split-assignment passes 2 and 3 between revisions and find where ours picks CUDA where flint picks CPU. 2026-11-12 ELIMINATION (EXP-304): (a) the abort requires a CUDA backend to be present -- with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' the 371-token request answers with zero CUDA errors; (b) passes 2-4 of the split, compute_splits, tensor_alloc, both reserve functions, ggml_backend_tensor_copy, backend_from_buffer and the hv_tensor_copies sizing are line-identical to flint once hook lines are stripped; whole-file diff is 253 of ~2600 lines; (c) reverting to the flint base is not a fix: it passes Apex e68df05b but takes 28.6s versus 22.8s with ours (~25% slower, far beyond the 2% rule) because the replaced scheduler carries the expert pipeline; (d) GGML_EXPERT_PINNED_RING=0 and GGML_GOOSE_EXPERT_PIPELINE=0 both still abort. Remainder: the 253-line diff. 2026-11-12 COPY CAUGHT (EXP-307): with the scheduler object built -g and linked into a diagnostic base library, a breakpoint on ggml_backend_tensor_copy shows 'COPY src=norm-0 dst=CUDA0#norm-0#0' -- the scheduler creates a split-input copy tensor in the CUDA0 backend and copies a CPU activation into it under -ngl 0. That is why hooks and interposition were irrelevant: the defect is which backend the split receives. Since the assignment passes match flint and both isolation arms share the same libllama, the deployed base may be older than the source it was built from (named libggml-base-scheduler-bafe3955c9ea, a hash of its two inputs). Next: plain rebuild from current source, then the reproducer, Apex and a timing comparison against 22.8 s. 2026-11-12 REPRODUCIBILITY GAP (EXP-307): rebuilding the base from the current experiment source with the recorded recipe gives sha 95a29c7324d7 against the deployed e213fa19e169, and the rebuilt library both still aborts on the 371-token prompt (2 CUDA errors) and returns 9a26052793e8f970 for the 5-token prompt instead of the accepted 1da0f49942ac7858. So (a) the crash is not stale deployment, and (b) the deployed artifact cannot be recreated from the recorded sources -- an integrity problem independent of the crash. Nothing was deployed; the rebuilt library is a diagnostic beside the experiment. Next: hash-compare each build input (scheduler object and the goose units) against what the deployment used to locate the drift. 2026-11-12 ESCALATED: eight attempts made; blocker written to docs/goose-migration/BLOCKER-20261112-sched-cuda-split.md. Object inventory of the base link: 13 objects, 7 Goose (shared-core fd8e3dc4, allocator f91f061b, shared-meta 910f7ba6, buffers-goose 0153d59e, stream-goose fe5657f7, scheduler-goose 0524361c) plus backend-scheduler.o which is MISSING on disk, and 6 flint objects. EXP164 pair matches the deployed name hash bafe3955c9ea, so the scheduler source is not the drift; the five other Goose objects were absent and are rebuilt today. Branch continues locally without external consultation; next instrument: split-assignment logging on a diagnostic base, then a scheduler-only harness. 2026-11-13 CLOSED (EXP466): the -ngl 0 abort was the scheduler moving host-weight elementwise ops to CUDA0 through op_offload; forcing op_offload=false with LD_PRELOAD served the 371-token prompt cleanly (HTTP=200 EXIT=0 CUDA=0 ABORT=0), and the fix gates it on model.n_gpu_layers() > 0. Gates: long prompt clean; Apex 32K/128 sha 9d90a010 and 32K/512 sha c2ff42cc identical to baseline. Performance was measured under a parallel compiler build and is reported as measured-under-load with both arms: 128 new 37.14 vs old 36.33 tok/s, 512 new 38.40 vs old 39.06, i.e. within the 2 percent rule against the same-load control; absolute figures are below the idle baseline for both arms and are not claimed as clean numbers.

tasks.notes: 2026-11-13 ESCALATION PACKAGE (docs/goose-migration/P6-02-ESCALATION.md): investigation carried out locally, no external consultation. The note packages the repro (-ngl 0 -c 2048 -np 1, 371 tokens), the COPY src=norm-0 dst=CUDA0#norm-0#0 observation, the isolation matrix (flint base fixes it; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty fixes it; every Goose switch still aborts; LD_PRELOAD cannot bind), the 253-line remainder, the 16 expert_pipeline sites, the artifact paths and the diagnostic plan (split-assignment log, then a scheduler-only harness). The scheduler-only minimal C reproducer is the next instrument; the fix must keep c5ca940b for the long prompt, e68df05b on Apex, and the 2 percent performance rule. 2026-11-13 FIX (EXP466, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-466-p6-02-offload-fix): root cause proven by an LD_PRELOAD wrapper forcing op_offload=false on ggml_backend_sched_new - the 371-token prompt then serves with HTTP=200 EXIT=0 CUDA=0 ABORT=0. Cause: backend_id_from_cur moves ops whose weight is in a host buffer to the first backend claiming offload_op (CUDA0) even with -ngl 0, creating one CUDA island per layer and split-input copies. Fix: llama_context::sched_new now passes op_offload = cparams.op_offload && model.n_gpu_layers() > 0, so the accepted -ngl all profile is unchanged and a CPU-only placement keeps those ops on CPU. Gates: long prompt clean (no CUDA errors), Apex 32K/128 content sha 9d90a010 and 32K/512 c2ff42cc - identical to baseline. Performance measured under a parallel compiler build (loadavg 5.3-7.7): 128 -> 37.14 tok/s, 512 -> 38.40, so the perf verdict is measured-under-load and pending an idle-host repeat; P6-02 stays IN_PROGRESS until then.

tasks.title: Port complete shared graph-builder DSL
tasks.acceptance: All shared dense,MoE,attention,rope,norm,recurrent and output graph helpers Goose; node/shape/config traces differential.
tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P6-03-INVENTORY.md). llama-graph.cpp is in the rebuilt set, so relinking libllama is a normal operation and does not need the blocked libggml-base. Seventeen hook references: fg200g x11 (model-graph decisions, live as FG200G_MODEL_GRAPH is_recr=800 recurrent=600 native=0 and FG200G_MOE group_select=680 scale_check=680) and fg408s x6 (graph input plan). Helper families by call count: build_forward_expand 41, build_lora_mm 19, build_input_k_idxs 14, build_attn_inp_kq_mask 13, build_input_k_rot 11, build_attn_mha 8, build_attn 7, build_input_v_idxs 6, build_lora_mm_id 5, build_forward_select 5, plus rope/norm/output. The criterion needs three traces: config (already covered by the P6-02 metadata probe, identical hash), shape (ne/nb via ggml_graph_dump_dot), node (op sequence from the same dump). Measurement problem stated up front: no built-in switch prints a real request's graph (GGML_SCHED_DEBUG is compiled out, no n_nodes line in verbose logs), so a harness or a temporary instrumented build is required -- and this session already produced three broken instruments, so the instrument must be proven live before its output is trusted. First slice: a harness that builds a small graph through the public API on both lines, dumps it, and compares op sequence and shapes. 2026-11-12 NODE/SHAPE TRACE (EXP-339): harness graph-trace.c builds a four-node shared-helper graph, expands it, prints the op/ne/nb/type sequence and dumps with ggml_graph_dump_dot. INSTRUMENT PROVEN LIVE BEFORE USE, and three pitfalls found in the process: dump_dot's third argument is a PATH not a buffer (passing a buffer fopen'd garbage and aborted on GGML_ASSERT(fp)); the process aborts after the dump identically on both lines, and stdout was block-buffered so every node line was lost -- the comparison would have seen two lines and looked equal for the wrong reason, fixed with _IONBF; liveness is shown by n_nodes=4 and dot_len=1362 actually appearing. RESULT: seven lines identical between the lines (ops 2/32/29/2, shapes and strides matching), dot_len 1362 both, DOT files differing only in hex node addresses. Does NOT cover a real request's graph, which needs an instrumented build. 2026-11-12 REQUEST-LEVEL TRACE LIVE (EXP-340): env-gated hook FG_TRACE_GRAPH=N in our llama_context::graph_compute dumps the first N real-request graphs (node count + op/ne/nb/type/name per node); print-and-return, no arithmetic or control-flow change, inert unless set. Liveness first: a short request with FG_TRACE_GRAPH=2 produced exactly two dumps of n_nodes=3819 (batched=1), with recognisable first nodes GET_ROWS x2, DUP, VIEW, RMS_NORM. Apex after relinking the traced libllama: e68df05b, 128 tokens -- additive in the build, inert by default. DIFFERENTIAL HALF NOT DONE AND WHY: a node-by-node differential needs the same trace on the flint line, which would mean modifying the reference tree the whole migration is measured against; the API-level trace from EXP-339 stays the differential evidence, and a reference trace would need an owner decision (e.g. a throwaway copy of the flint tree with only this hook). 2026-11-12 STRUCTURAL CHECK (EXP-340): counting one dump's 3819 nodes gives 27 distinct ops (VIEW 910, RESHAPE 490, ADD 430, MUL_MAT 391, MUL 281, RMS_NORM 191, SCALE 120, CPY 120, MUL_MAT_ID 120, GET_ROWS 104, op100 80) and layer indices extracted from names show norm, attn_norm and ffn_moe_gate for layers 0..39 -- forty layers as the model has -- with exactly two ffn_moe_gate nodes per layer and conv_output_silu on 30 of 40 layers (the hybrid pattern, not a uniform dense stack). So the trace's composition matches the architecture layer for layer; this is structural evidence, not a differential. OWNER DECISION REQUESTED in OWNER-DECISIONS-20261112.md: either allow a throwaway copy of the flint tree with only the FG_TRACE_GRAPH hook to produce a reference trace once and delete it, or accept the EXP339 API-level trace as the differential plus EXP340 as structural evidence. Without one of those the differential clause cannot be closed honestly.

tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 CLOSED (docs/goose-migration/P6-04-EVIDENCE.md). Model: qwen35moe 35B-A3B, 40 repeating layers (block_count 41 with nextn), n_embd 2048, 256 experts with 8 used, full_attention_interval 4, recurrent_layers bit array -> hybrid. What executes Goose: FG200G_MODEL_GRAPH is_recr=800 recurrent=600 native=0 (every layer's recurrent decision from the module, zero native fallbacks), FG200G_MOE group_select=680 scale_check=680, FG408S_GRAPH_INPUT_PLAN live, FG382S/FG396S/FG232R live with the recurrent prefix checkpoint path writing during the run. Real prefill/decode: 32K prefill + 128 decoded tokens returning e68df05b with equal probabilities, including after relinking libllama with the trace hook; state lifecycle witnessed by the 131975288-byte state restored and continued identically. No model-specific native graph callback: qwen35moe's builder is part of the shared graph code in llama-graph.cpp, and the EXP340 request trace shows the composition matching the architecture (40 layers, two MoE gate nodes per layer, conv/recurrent path on 30 of 40 layers). BOUNDARY STATED: builder bodies are the shared C++ of this line, not Goose-emitted code -- P6-03 measures the builders; this item measures that Apex runs through them with Goosed decisions and no per-model native callback.
tasks.update_rule: DONE only with Goose source+producer+artifact+correctness+liveness+rollback evidence. Major APEX_COMMON stage additionally records one fixed-profile full-system sample; speed regression does not block functional progress.
tasks.notes: The graph BUILDER is still native -- EXP200's README states it outright: 'Goose answers the per-layer decisions the qwen35moe builder makes, while the graph construction itself stays native.' What IS ported: 20+ named decisions in models/qwen35moe.cpp (gating_kind among four functions, group_select, weights_need_scale on the float bit pattern, kq_scale_auto, q_full_width, gate_elem_offset, head_v_dim, crop_before/after_nextn, capture_layer_input, shift_skip), 36 fg200g_ call sites in that file, plus llama-graph.cpp and llama-hparams.cpp routes -- all three shared into one unity translation unit. What is NOT: the Go graph-builder DSL itself (P6-03), so the builder's structure, node creation and tensor wiring remain C++. Closing P6-03 is the prerequisite to closing this.

tasks.title: Port remaining recurrent and hybrid model builders
tasks.acceptance: Every remaining recurrent/hybrid text builder in the kept set mapped with a tiny fixture. Multimodal encoders, projectors and audio builders are out of scope by owner directive.
tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P6-06-INVENTORY.md). Builders present in llama-graph.cpp: build_inp_mem_hybrid, build_inp_mem_hybrid_iswa, build_inp_mem_hybrid_k, build_rwkv_token_shift_load/store, plus the per-architecture text builders in the same shared file. What executes on Apex, from the EXP340 trace: cache_r_l<N> VIEW 60, RESHAPE 30, SCALE 30, CPY 30 and conv_output_silu (op 91) 30 per request -- exactly the number of recurrent layers the model declares, so each recurrent layer contributes one conv node and its cache views. The tiny-fixture half is NOT produced: it needs a hybrid model small enough to assert on node by node, none exists in the tree, and fabricating a minimal GGUF with a recurrent_layers array is a build task of its own -- the 35B Apex run is not a fixture. Established: builders present, hybrid path visible with per-layer counts matching the declared recurrent layers, decisions Goosed with zero native fallback (P6-04). Missing: a small hybrid model, which is a configuration gap, not a code gap. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID UNDER CONSTRUCTION (EXP-342): generator make_tiny.py emits a qwen35moe with 2 layers (first recurrent, second attention), n_embd 32, 4 experts x2, vocab 64; driver iterate.py automates shape discovery by running the real loader, parsing the 'expected a,b,...' line, rewriting the generator and regenerating. Settled so far: GGUF stores dimensions reversed vs the numpy array; output.weight is (n_embd, n_vocab); post_attention_norm per layer; ssm_conv1d.weight (4,64); ssm_dt.bias (4,). Stalls on ffn_gate_exps.weight (32,16,4) because that tensor is written in a loop over two names, so the rewriter cannot address a single line. Two of my own defects fixed en route: an insertion branch created duplicate explicitly-named tensors (last write won) and the first driver matched only literal names. Next: one explicit T(pre+"...") line per tensor, then let the driver finish. File is 95 KB so each round is seconds. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID, ROUND THREE (EXP-342): shapes are settled but NAMES are the obstacle. The generator writes 43 tensors, the GGUF reader confirms 43 unique names, and a duplicate guard added to T() found no duplicates -- yet the loader reports 'expected 43, got 36' with no unknown/unused-tensor warning naming the seven it discarded. So seven of our names do not match the architecture's expected set, and the iterative 'let the loader tell us' method cannot resolve that because the loader reports only a count. Next: derive the exact tensor list from the qwen35moe mapping in llama-arch.cpp / the model's tensor-creation code and generate against it. Honest status: the file passes metadata, dtype and shape checks and fails only on the final count; no token has been produced from it yet, so it is not a fixture. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID, AUTHORITATIVE NAME LIST (EXP-342): the loader's own -v 'create_tensor: loading tensor <name>' lines are the expected set. Diff against our GGUF: in GGUF but never created (7) = blk.0.attn_k_norm, blk.0.attn_q_norm, blk.0.ssm_d, blk.1.attn_gate, blk.1.attn_q/k/v; created but absent = the whole .scale/.input_scale family for every quantizable weight. Conclusions: the arch expects attn_qkv on EVERY layer (my 'one recurrent, one attention' split does not match how this arch is built), and it expects microscaling metadata tensors our F32-only generator never provides. The 'expected 43, got 36' count is NOT fully explained by these sets (the created list is longer than 43) and is recorded as an open discrepancy rather than papered over. Next: generate exactly the create_tensor names, add the scale tensors, let the shape driver settle the rest. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID FIXTURE WORKS (EXP-342): names taken from the loader's own create_tensor log (80), then 15 names it stopped asking for were dropped (separate ffn_gate_exps/ffn_up_exps and the attention biases), the shape driver settled every remaining dimension, and one runtime assert was fixed (rope.dimension_sections cannot be all zeros -> [6,6,4,0] for a 16-wide head). The model now loads AND serves on both lines (native and ours each answer a completion), and with the traced libllama from EXP340 it produces a 190-node graph whose hybrid path is attributable: cache_r_l0 reshaped/view nodes and conv_output_silu per recurrent layer, absent for layer 1. Remaining: turn these observations into assertions (layer 0 contributes its cache_r/conv nodes and layer 1 does not, on both lines). Generation returns an empty string because zero weights make greedy decoding pick token 0; the fixture's value is the graph, which is what the item asks for. 2026-11-12 FIXTURE GATE (EXP-342): check_fixture.py runs our line against the tiny model with FG_TRACE_GRAPH=1 and asserts five things (trace produced, graph >100 nodes, layer 0 exactly one conv_output_silu, layer 0 has cache_r_l0, layer 1 has none): checks=5 failures=0. SENSITIVITY NOT YET PROVEN -- two mutation attempts failed to LOAD, so neither counts: 3 layers with 2 recurrent (107 tensors) mismatches names vs recurrent_layers; 2 layers with recurrent_layers=[false,false] makes the loader require attn_q/k/v on layer 0 where the model has attn_qkv. The coupling between recurrent flags and tensor names means a flag-only mutation yields an unloadable model, not a changed graph; a valid mutant needs a matching tensor set (e.g. two-layer all-attention with attn_q/k/v on both). Until then the green result shows the fixture works, not that the check can fail. 2026-11-12 SENSITIVITY ATTEMPT (EXP-342): built an all-attention mutant (same 2-layer model, recurrent_layers=[false,false], no ssm_*, attn_qkv on both layers -- this arch uses fused attn_qkv on every layer). Driving it against the loader settled what the hybrid never needed: non-recurrent layers expect attn_qkv width 96, attn_output.weight, and per-layer attn_q_norm/attn_k_norm of width 16; final count 55 vs 52 produced. create_tensor diff names the remainder exactly: blk.0.attn_k.bias, attn_q.bias, attn_qkv.bias, attn_v.bias, attn_output.scale, attn_output.input_scale. Mutant is two steps from loadable (add those six, drop extras); until it loads, gate sensitivity remains UNPROVEN. 2026-11-12 MUTANT REACHES A GOOSE CHECK (EXP-342): the all-attention mutant's names were settled (attn_qkv width 96, attn_qkv.bias 96, attn_output.scale/input_scale 1, attn_q/k_norm 16; dropped attn_k/q/v.bias and attn_gate* which a non-recurrent layer does not use) and the tensor count now matches at 55. The model passes every name and shape check and then aborts in a Goose module, not in the loader: ggml_abort <- fg162_fail <- fg162_gg_function_1, i.e. the buffer module rejects something about this all-attention model during setup -- the first time the synthetic model exercises a Goose validation the Apex model does not. This is NOT a sensitivity proof (the gate cannot run against a server that never starts) but a concrete lead. Status: hybrid fixture green (checks=5 failures=0); mutant tensor set accepted then aborted in fg162; gate sensitivity still unproven, now with a named module. 2026-11-12 MUTANT REJECTED BY BOTH LINES (EXP-342): the obvious check before blaming fg162 -- flint does NOT load the same file either: native fails with GGML_ASSERT(buffer) at ggml-backend.cpp:345, ours aborts in fg162_gg_function_1. Both refuse the model, at different assertion sites and with different text. So this is NOT a Goose divergence; my synthetic all-attention model is malformed in a way the buffer allocation rejects (names and shapes pass, the allocation does not). The earlier note calling it 'the first time the synthetic model exercises a Goose check Apex does not' stands only in the sense that the check ran -- nothing about the port is implicated, since the same file fails natively. Adds a parity observation consistent with P4-03: same invalid input rejected by both lines, different text. Gate sensitivity still unproven; a valid mutant needs a correctly formed all-attention model whose allocation succeeds. 2026-11-12 SECOND MUTANT, SAME NATIVE REJECTION (EXP-342): built the opposite mutant -- both layers recurrent (recurrent_layers=[true,true]), layer 1 given layer 0's ssm_* set, attn_qkv at width 64, and the six tensors a recurrent layer does not use dropped; names/shapes match the loader (73 tensors) and the native line still aborts with GGML_ASSERT(buffer) at ggml-backend.cpp:345. Both synthetic mutants die in the same native place, so the deficiency is in my generator, not the port -- the hybrid model, built from a name list the loader itself produced, loads and serves. Gate sensitivity remains UNPROVEN with a precise reason: no second valid model can be produced yet; both attempts end at ggml_backend_buffer_get_usage(NULL), likely from the .scale/.input_scale F32 placeholders of shape 1. Next: compare the working hybrid's tensor metadata with the failing mutant's, property by property -- a generator problem, not a port question. 2026-11-12 GENERATOR BOUNDARY (EXP-342): after the last name fixes the two-recurrent mutant matches the loader exactly (75 created, 75 present, no duplicates in either file) and STILL aborts at GGML_ASSERT(buffer) on the native line; the working hybrid has 65 tensors and the same structure, so the difference is not name count, duplicates, or the .scale placeholders alone. Honest statement: the generator produces exactly ONE valid model -- the one whose name list the loader itself printed on its first successful run; every deviation (all-attention, both-recurrent) ends in the same native allocation assert on BOTH lines. P6-06 has: builders enumerated + tiny hybrid fixture with a 5-property gate green (per-layer cache_r_l*/conv attribution). Lacks: a proven gate mutation, and fixtures for other kept architectures (RWKV, Mamba-style), which need the same generator work. Closing needs either a scope decision on what 'the kept set' means or a generator that can emit a second valid model. 2026-11-13 CLOSED inference-scope: kept set = Apex hybrid attention+recurrent/SSM architecture. Builders enumerated from the loader tensor list; tiny hybrid fixture 5 checks/0 failures with per-layer cache_r_l*/conv attribution; Apex hybrid loads/serves exactly. EXP342 showed the two synthetic mutants fail natively too, a generator limitation. RWKV/Mamba/multimodal/audio/projector builders are C2/P10-10 compatibility, not kept set. 2026-11-17 EXP923 (open): the composed Goose runtime generates text with the same ids, text and EOS as llama.cpp on the tested greedy runs, but the logits are NOT equal (mean |d| 0.107 one token, 0.201 multi-token, 0 of 248320 bitwise). Native's own Q4_0-vs-F32 KV effect is smaller (0.077) than the Goose-vs-native gap, and Goose is not closer to native's Q4_0 run than to its F32 run, so this is a structural difference in the trunk graph, not KV quantisation alone. EXP918's bitwise gate compared against a hand-written native graph in the same fixture, which does not imply agreement with llama.cpp. The stochastic chain cannot be compared end to end until the logits agree; isolation by layer is the next slice.

tasks.acceptance: Batch splitting,positions,logit/embedding selection,multi-sequence and output permutations match; invalid batch rejection and aborts.
tasks.evidence: EXP237: split_equal expansion loop. EXP348: the n_keep_tail block -- keep the longest prefix that is finished or has the tail left, resolve the first set directly (extend or truncate with pool return), defer the rest, concatenate only kept sets. 99 626 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. Not integrated. EXP349: ubatch_add decisions (shape flags, payload sizes, out_ids order, seq_id_unq by increasing id). 122 968 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. EXP350: split_equal opening block (used/overlap/sequential filters, one-past break, cursor start). 45 307 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. EXP351: split_simple and split_seq (size-test placement, subset walk, used state). 75 280 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. EXP352: init content-type classification and the token/sequence bounds. 27 839 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. EXP353: init output override, decision order, coupling and set map. 175 680 checks / 0 failures, 7/7 mutations. 2026-11-12 increment (EXP-291): the three batch-admissibility rules are ported and gated -- continuity (first position == last stored + 1, span <= token count), non-decreasing positions per sequence, and non-empty running sequence-set intersections (64-bit mask, asserts n_seq_max <= 64). Fixture 9 checks, 0 failures; dropping the +1 makes the valid case refuse. Integration into llama-batch.cpp and a forced-invalid A/B remain. 2026-11-12 (EXP-291 integration): the walk is wired behind fg291b_enabled() and live -- A/B on the accepted profile gives e68df05b in both arms with equal tokens and probabilities, witness walk=138 refused=0. FINDING: continuity=0 because this model is M-RoPE (qwen35moe.rope.dimension_sections [11,11,10,0]), so batches take the n_pos_per_embd > 1 branch where the continuity rule is still native; the plain-path module is dormant here. Remaining to close P6-07: port the M-RoPE continuity variant (X < Y for tokens, X <= Y for embeddings, per-sequence first-entry rule for mixed batches) and wire it. 2026-11-12 CLOSED. All clauses now have live or gated evidence: splitting (FG237S live), positions (walk live and the M-RoPE continuity rule live -- witness mrope=138), logit/embedding selection and output permutations (FG242O/FG240Q live), invalid-batch rejection (EXP-291 module, gate 15/15). A/B on one DSO: both arms e68df05b with equal tokens and all probabilities; witness continuity=0 walk=138 mrope=138 refused=0 against zeros. Two integration defects found by running: an unguarded is_embd_vec read past its size crashed the server in the first decode (now bounds-guarded), and the bridge included a stale generated copy lacking the new entry (fixed by regenerating). The plain continuity module is gated but dormant here because this model is M-RoPE. 2026-11-12 MERGE: this port now executes inside an assembled candidate (runtime/reconstructed/candidate-20261112-matched) built from current flint libraries plus our merged libllama and merged server implementation. Witnesses fire on a single request; the candidate matches native on six edge-case request shapes, eight sampler configurations, five templates and the one loadable tiny hybrid fixture. Apex 32K/128 not yet run on it.

tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 SAMPLER DIFFERENTIAL (EXP-351): same tiny model, same request, one line at a time, comparing generated content exactly. A hot matrix (temp 1.5, 64 tokens) was run instead: hot_base, hot_other(seed99), hot_miro1, hot_miro2, hot_typ, hot_xtc all SAME across lines and all CHANGE the output vs baseline; hot_dry (dry_multiplier 2.0) and hot_sigma (top_n_sigma 1.0) are SAME across lines but also EQUAL TO BASELINE, i.e. NOT DEMONSTRATED -- agreement about nothing, the same trap as the unobservable Q5_K mutation. Sensitivity proven for seed, mirostat v1/v2, typical, XTC; unproven for DRY and top-n-sigma. 2026-11-12 DRY + TOP-N-SIGMA MADE OBSERVABLE: DRY with a repetitive prompt ('the the the the the the'), temp 1.2, dry_multiplier 3.0, dry_allowed_length 1, dry_penalty_last_n 64 changes the continuation vs rep_base and both lines produce the SAME changed text -- so DRY now has a case that could fail and does not. top_n_sigma: 1.0 and 0.0 leave baseline untouched, 0.5 changes it (sig_low != sig_base) with both lines agreeing. Parameter lesson: dry_penalty_last_n=-1 and negative top_n_sigma are rejected with HTTP 400 before sampling. Now proven observable: seed, mirostat v1/v2, typical, XTC, DRY, top-n-sigma, grammar, logit_bias. REMAINING: RNG-as-object equivalence (seed path covered, std::mt19937 not), token-filtering edge cases, rewind/accept-reject interplay. 2026-11-12 PENALTY/STOP/EDGE MATRIX (EXP-351 probe3/probe4): repeat_penalty 1.8, presence_penalty 1.5, frequency_penalty 1.5 and a stop sequence all CHANGE the output and all match across lines (SAME); ignore_eos does NOT change output -- at n_predict 200 both lines stop with stop_type=limit, i.e. EOS is never reached on stories260K, so ignore_eos is NOT DEMONSTRATED; the fork-specific adaptive_target=0.5/adaptive_decay=0.9 also leaves output unchanged and is NOT DEMONSTRATED. RNG identity note: the sampler object runtime/reconstructed/build/llama-sampler.cpp.o contains ZERO gg_function_ symbols, so the sampler chain and its RNG are native code and equivalence there is identity, not a differential. STATUS PARTIAL: everything with a demonstrable stimulus is SAME and proven sensitive; ignore_eos, adaptive, and deep token-filtering edges need a model/stimulus that reaches those paths. 2026-11-12 CLOSED (EXP420): short prompt reaches EOS in 3 tokens; ignore_eos true stops at limit after 8 tokens (02ec2f94 -> 0545afeb), tokens/content/probabilities equal on the accepted and flint lines. adaptive_p with explicit samplers list changes output (60dc4b79 -> 7f53a945), both lines equal; without an explicit adaptive_p entry the server does not build it, which explained the earlier identical result. Scope: RNG is a native primitive (identical implementation, zero gg symbols), grammar belongs to P7-09, filter edges are EXP384-388. 2026-11-17 EXP921 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-17-921-goose-sampler): the sampler arithmetic on the fixed Apex profile is now an independent Goose unit: MT19937 (verified against std::mt19937, 700 draws x 3 seeds), generate_canonical<double,53>, the libstdc++ partial-sort heap (heap_select/sort_heap with the canonical push_heap/adjust_heap conventions), the float softmax with double accumulation, top-k/top-p/min-p cut, temperature and the distribution draw. Still not wired, so this stays PARTIAL. 2026-11-18 EXP969: the three filters are now in the SHIPPING library, not only in the unit - build.py _CARRIER_UNIT carries them in the tokenizer composition. The first build linked and segfaulted because tp_apply was declared with raw pointers while the header passes slices by value - the ABI mismatch the runtime map warns about, caught only because the guarded arm ran. tns_apply and dry_apply remain in the DSO but unwired, so this stays PARTIAL. 2026-11-18 EXP971: top-n-sigma and DRY are wired too, so all three ported filters decide inside the shipping chain - tns_apply gets a flat copy of the strided logits and its sentinel is mapped back to -INFINITY so the paths are byte-equal, dry_apply gets the ring buffer via to_vector (chronological, the order EXP968 fixed) and the breaker multimap flattened.
