The oracle is common_chat_template_direct_apply with generation_params{add_bos, add_eos, mark_input}, because common_chat_templates_apply copies add_bos from the template and it is false without a model. Six cases cover literal vs input BOS/EOS in both positions. Gate: 593 cases / 1048 values / 0 failures, mutations 12/12 in two halves. Recorded approximations: marking is applied to the messages subtree rather than per from_json call, and filters do not propagate the flag yet, so filtered user content is treated as template text. The typed direction, grammars/autoparser, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's time injection remain. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP553 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-553-p7-08-flag-propagation): the input flag now survives filters. The native rules were taken from string.cpp/value.cpp rather than the header comment: apply_transform keeps the flag per part, replace/slice/indent call mark_input_based_on, string/safe return the value unchanged, tojson and join build a fresh unmarked string, split marks only the remaining tail (cut tokens are created before the marking call), and format takes the flag of the first non-empty rendered piece. The port adds inherit_input(src, dst) and calls it from those branches, with format recording the first piece while it builds. Two initial rules were disproved by the gate and corrected: join was marking when all elements were input (native never marks), and split was marking every token (native marks only the tail). Gate: 607 cases / 1076 values / 0 failures, mutations 14/14 in two halves (7+7). The remaining items are the typed direction, grammars/autoparser, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP554 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-554-p7-08-parts): the input flag is now two bits, matching the native part list. common/chat.cpp strips BOS/EOS from the first non-empty prompt part, while all_parts_are_input() is true only when every part is input and mark_input_based_on uses it. The difference shows in concatenation and format: content~'b' has an input first part but not every part, ''~content skips the empty part when choosing the first prompt part yet still zeroes the all flag, and format pushes literal pieces with fmt.all_parts_are_input() while argument pieces keep their own per-part flags. The port adds bit 32 (all parts input), keeps bit 16 (first part), uses mark_from_input for replace/slice/indent/split-tail, treats ~ and + as first-operand-part plus AND of both operands, and makes format track both the first emitted piece and the AND over pieces. The gate disproved two initial assumptions: an empty string does constrain the all flag (it has one empty part), and format literals are keyed off all_parts, not the format's first-part flag. Gate: 618 cases / 1098 values / 0 failures, mutations 14/14 in two halves (7+7). Part lists remain approximated by two bits per value, which the current templates do not distinguish further. The typed direction, grammars/autoparser, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection remain native. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP555 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-555-p7-08-parse-entry): the output-parse oracle is available without weights. common_chat_parse forwards to common_chat_peg_parse(params.parser, ...); the arena is built by common_chat_templates_apply from the template text and tools only, and common_chat_input(std::string) fills tokens with LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL, so common_chat_session(tmpls, nullptr, inputs) parses plain text without a vocabulary. A probe over the fixture templates shows every one reports format=peg-native and parser=present, so no real template takes the fallback and the PEG subsystem (chat-peg-parser.cpp, 1239 lines including the builder and AST mappers) is the true size of the remaining item. This slice ports the empty-arena path: a static content(rest())+end() grammar yields role=assistant and content = generation_prompt ++ text, because common_chat_input prepends the prompt before parsing. The port adds chat_parse_content_only(gp, text, out) and the fixture compares full OAI JSON against the native message over ten inputs. Gate: 628 cases / 1108 values / 0 failures, mutations 12/12 in two halves (two are detected by the runtime bounds check, stated in the card). Remaining: the PEG builder and chat grammar, the AST mappers, partial streaming, the typed direction, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP556 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-556-p7-08-peg-builder): the chat PEG builder is ported against common_peg_arena::dump. The native builder appends nodes (root is the last node), stores one contiguous child run per parent, and flattens a nested sequence into a sequence and a nested choice into a choice; tag helpers wrap their child in Tag(name, child) and tool_open/tool_close/tool_id/tool_name also wrap it in Atomic. The dump formats are Epsilon, End, Until(), Literal(text), Tag(name, child), Atomic(child), Sequence(...), Choice(...) and Repetition(child, min, unbounded). The port adds peg_rest/peg_end_node/peg_eps_node/peg_literal/peg_tag/peg_atomic/peg_seq/peg_choice/peg_repeat over the existing node model plus peg_dump_basic, with the same flattening. Gate: 646 cases / 1126 values / 0 failures over eighteen grammars, mutations 14/14 in two halves (7+7). Flattening was missing from the first attempt and the nested-sequence case caught it; one mutation is detected by a stack overflow rather than a value mismatch because the dump follows a bogus root, which the harness reports. The chat grammar composition, the standard JSON/XML tool builders, the AST mappers and partial streaming remain native, as do the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP557 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-557-p7-08-chat-grammar): the chat grammar helpers are ported and gated by arena dump. tag_with_safe_content(name, marker, p) is zero_or_more(choice({p, rule(name, content(negate(literal(marker)) + any + until(marker)))})), or content(any) without a marker; optspace(tag) starts from eps, adds one optional literal per leading space, the literal body and one optional per trailing space, and the flattened dump keeps the leading Epsilon; prefix(s, delimiter) is eps for an empty string, literal(s) without a delimiter and literal(s up to the delimiter) otherwise; the dump forms are Any, Not(child), Until(marker)/Until() and Rule(name, child). The port adds peg_any_node, peg_not_node, peg_until_marker, peg_rule_node, peg_optspace, peg_prefix, peg_tag_safe and explicit-children helpers. Compiler finding: an exported function cannot be called both from the C fixture and from Goose code (could not resolve one concrete function signature, reported at the export declaration), so peg_literal/peg_tag/peg_seq/peg_choice are split into a private _impl plus an exported wrapper. Gate: 662 cases / 1142 values / 0 failures over sixteen grammars, mutations 14/14 in two halves (7+7). The tool builders (standard_json_tools, standard_constructed_tools, permute), the AST mappers and partial streaming remain native, as do the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP559 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-559-p7-08-permute): permute is ported. Empty input is eps, one parser or more than six falls back to a sequence, and otherwise every subset of remaining parsers becomes a rule named prefix-mask whose body is a choice of parser i followed by the subset without i; the root is the full mask. Native creates a fresh eps per zero subset, wraps even a single alternative in a Choice, and shares subset rules, so the dump prints [cycle] on a second visit and Tag re-dumps its child with a fresh visited set. The port walks masks upwards, caches rules by mask, and extends the dump with two visited sets and the cycle marker. Three first-attempt differences were caught by the gate: a bare sequence instead of a single-alternative choice, a shared zero-subset epsilon, and the missing visited sets. Gate: 672 cases / 1152 values / 0 failures over nine permute grammars, mutations 12/12 in two halves (6+6). The standard JSON/XML tool builders, the AST mappers and partial streaming remain native, as do the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP560 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-560-p7-08-mapper-port): the base AST mapper is ported. It is one preorder walk: content and reasoning append sanitized text with no separator, whitespace-only reasoning is dropped after the walk, trim() removes at most one leading and every trailing space, tool-open starts a fresh pending call, tool-id strips one pair of quotes, tool-name flushes args_buffer or opens with '{' and pushes the call immediately, arg-name writes a quoted key and ':', arg-value appends normalize_quotes_to_json, a schema-declared string value appends escaped text inside quotes closed by arg-close, and tool-close closes a pending quote and unclosed braces by depth. The draft came from a helper agent and was rebuilt and re-run here before use. The gate builds the same grammar on both sides, parses with the ported arena and compares role, content, reasoning, call count and every name/arguments/id: 16 pairs, 87 values, mutations 12/12 in two halves (6+6). Recorded approximations: one shared tool buffer needs a high-water cursor; escaping does not validate UTF-8; normalize_quotes uses ASCII word characters; capacity is the caller's contract; the final pending flush and model-parser-only tool-arg-string-value are unreachable from the base mapper; arguments are never re-marshalled. gemma4/minimax mappers, partial streaming, the tool builders, the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection remain native. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP561 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-561-p7-08-visited-depth): the dump visited sets are fixed by Tag depth. Native keeps one visited set that accumulates and is never cleared on return, while entering Tag starts a new empty set and leaving it leaves the parent untouched. EXP559 modelled that with two arrays chosen by slot parity, which breaks at Tag depth 2: the counter and the array drift apart, so a [cycle] can disappear. The fix uses one array with a base index: lookup only in vis[vbase..cursor), append at the cursor, children keep the base, and Tag records the cursor, walks with that base and restores it. Also recorded honestly: EXP560 was built on a pre-EXP559 copy of the canonical runtime, so its commit dropped permute and the cycle-aware dump; this slice rebuilds the canonical file from the EXP559 runtime, adds the EXP560 mapper and applies the fix, gated on both permute and depth constructions. Gate: 678 cases / 1158 values / 0 failures over six new depth constructions (repeat in one tag, across a tag boundary, at depths 2, 4 and 5, shared subtree outside a nested tag), mutations 12/12 in two halves (6+6). The tool builders, gemma4/minimax mappers, partial streaming, the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection remain native. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP562 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-562-p7-08-subclass-mappers): the gemma4 and MiniMax-M3 mappers are ported. Both stop the walk at content/reasoning/tool, so nested tagged text is not emitted twice (unlike the base arena.visit); find_by_tag searches to depth 3. gemma4 uses the name without trimming, rejects a partial name, takes arguments from the first child of tool-args and never reads id; minimax has no partial check on the name, builds arguments from the whole tool node as a container with closed = !node.is_partial, and skips a tool-arg without a name. Neither calls the base from_ast, so whitespace-only reasoning is not cleaned. The draft came from a helper agent and was rebuilt and re-run before use. Gate: 13 hand-built AST pairs / 65 values / 0 failures (partial cases G3, G4, G5, G10, M2), mutations 12/12 in two halves (6+6). Recorded approximations: the draft's g_* helpers still use a flat ABI that differs from the base target buffer; JSON escaping does not validate UTF-8; two upstream quirks are copied (an empty string child does not close its quote, an empty container prints nothing); minimax can emit a truncated streamed name; the gate uses oracle-captured JSON and synthetic ids, so a real arena also needs the sdir mapping and service tags must stay out of tid. Partial streaming, the tool builders, the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, use_jinja=false and the chat API's missing time injection remain native. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP563 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-563-p7-08-legacy): the legacy use_jinja=false path is ported. The oracle needs no weights: probe links the real src/llama-chat.cpp and reproduces the wrapper from src/llama.cpp verbatim, probe2 calls common_chat_templates_apply with use_jinja=false/true and prints every common_chat_params field. Detection matches 55/55 names; prompts match 34 template + 39 targeted + 2 content-part cases byte for byte. The port adds legacy_detect, legacy_apply and the builders for all 55 formats, including the 19 that the first draft left as gap codes (deepseek-ocr, chatglm4, minicpm, exaone3/4/moe, rwkv-world, megrez, smolvlm, dots1, hunyuan-moe/dense/vl, gpt-oss, grok-2, bailing and others). Gate: 75/75 prompts, detection 55/55, mutations 18/18 in two halves (9+9). Differences recorded: the legacy path ignores tools/tool_calls/reasoning_content and keeps format CONTENT_ONLY, emits no generation_prompt/parser/delimiters, ignores add_bos/add_eos, uses C isspace in trim, and copies the upstream content-part newline duplication. The oracle is linked from the flint tree, so goldens must be regenerated if it moves. The tool builders, partial streaming, the typed direction, autoparser/grammars, model parsers and the chat API's missing time injection remain. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP564 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-564-p7-08-typed): the typed-content direction is ported. EXP537 recorded the only_typed branch as untestable, but it is reachable through common_chat_templates_apply with a custom template (content[0]) and through jinja::caps_get; common_chat_msgs_to_json_oaicompat gives the exact JSON in both shapes. The port adds chat_content_parts_caps_json and chat_content_string_caps_json: arrays become a string under only_string, strings become one text part under only_typed, media always forces the string form, unknown part types stay in the array form, and empty content yields "". Concatenation and the media scan are reused from the canonical runtime. Gate: 24 pairs / 34 values / 0 failures, mutations 21/21 in two halves (11+10). Findings: native writes raw UTF-8, escapes control bytes as lowercase \u00XX, keeps 0x7f raw and throws type_error.316 on invalid UTF-8, so the draft's \xNN escaper was replaced by the canonical escaper plus a strict UTF-8 check; the compact separators are the byte contract. The canonical runtime still has a second escaper (esc with \xNN) used by chat_content_json, chat_message_full_json and chat_tools_json; unifying them is a separate slice. Tool calls in the typed path, legacy content merging, autoparser/grammars, model parsers, partial streaming and the chat API's missing time injection remain. P7-08 remains PARTIAL. 2026-11-14 EXP566 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-566-p7-08-delimiters): token-aligned message delimiters are ported. add/tokenize/split semantics: empty markers are skipped, the first marker in insertion order wins at a position, skip regions (media) are jumped over, content before the first match is dropped, the last span runs to the end, is_user_start is true only at an exact start, and last_user_message_pos returns the last user span. The port has build_msg_delims/dl_add, dl_bind_tokens/dl_bind_all, dl_split, sp_is_user_start, sp_last_user_pos, role_from_string/to_string and an incremental start probe; the caller tokenizes and passes ids, so the module has no external C symbol. Gate: 36 cases / 1452 values / 0 failures over 10 fixed tables, 10 real templates through autoparser::analyze_template, 8 edge cases, 7 native split-corpus cases and one contract case; mutations 12/12 in two halves (6+6). The server_tokens linkage group is deferred because get_tokens() aborts without a constructed server session; that is recorded, not approximated. The canonical runtime source is now EXP566 and check-goose-tree verifies it byte-for-byte against the experiment. 2026-11-14 EXP567 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-567-p7-08-streaming): the chat session layer is ported. feed appends the chunk, parses the whole text leniently and publishes only a monotone candidate; a failed parse with end>0 keeps the previous message, end==0 freezes the session, finish marks the session finished before parsing and a bad tail is a protocol error. compute_diffs accepts suffix growth of reasoning and content, a non-shrinking call count, a prefix name and appended calls. The port adds chat_stream_open, chat_stream_step, chat_msg_diff, chat_msg_monotone and chat_stream_error_name, validates the previous message table against its buffers (-5), keeps per-step and last-error status separate, and exposes a string table for the server layer. Gate: STREAM 10 cases/47 steps/271 values, DIFF 10/106, MONO 10/21/273, CONTRACT 13/15/61, CALLER 12/12, all zero failures; mutations 14/14 in two halves (7+7). The parser stays native: the gate feeds the step the native parse facts, so the session and publication layer is what is gated. The mapper is called through the export ABI because Goose cannot call an exported function with const slices internally. Freezing on a non-monotone tail is native behaviour. The caller contract is recorded in the experiment docs. The canonical runtime source is now EXP567. 2026-11-14 EXP569 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-569-p7-08-autoparser): the autoparser grammar generator is ported: content and reasoning sections, JSON_NATIVE, TAG_WITH_JSON and TAG_WITH_TAGGED tool formats (parallel on/off, function_is_key, nested keys, per-call wrappers, call-id PRE/POST), response-format fenced/plain, grammar decision (include/lazy/triggers), GBNF emission from the flat arena and preserved-token collection. Gate: 36/36 drafts, grammar 10/10, tools 8/8, tokens 6/6, hoist 4/4, plus the earlier slices 3/3, 10/10, 21/21, 29/29; mutations 12/12 in two halves. Recorded limits: hoisted rule names use a local pid and do not match native to_gbnf 0/4; Schema/response-format grammar is a stub (meta[3]=1); lazy root is not compared byte-wise; gates run at -O0 while the template expects -O1. The canonical runtime source is now EXP569 (16319 lines, +3087 over the previous canon). 2026-11-14 EXP570 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-570-p7-08-schema): the JSON-schema-to-GBNF converter is ported: the document walk ($ref, oneOf/anyOf, type arrays, const, enum, implicit kinds), object required/properties/additionalProperties, array items/prefixItems and tuples, string pattern/format and lengths, integer bounds with exclusive folding, uuid1..5, the cycle-safe ref map, the allOf merge with enum intersection, and the exact rejection text. Gate against json_schema_to_grammar at base e1238277: 30 cases / 182 values / 0 failures, mutations 12/12 in two halves. The corrected gate also found six defects in the integrated file (end-offset used as length, a pattern wrapper overreading by one byte, an unflushed literal on break, a shared trie reject slot, an allOf-enum cursor, and a fixture id pushed after recursion); all fixed minimally. The merged file keeps the EXP496 output helpers (format_grammar/check_errors), and EXP496 is now marked canonical so the sync no longer emits a duplicate format-grammar slot. Recorded limits: the gate runs at -O0 and values=182 follows the oracle version. 2026-11-14 EXP574 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-574-p7-08-tool-builders): the standard tool builders are ported onto the current canon - standard_json_tools and standard_constructed_tools with parallel on/off, function_is_key, nested dot keys, per-call wrappers, call-id PRE/POST, default and custom start markers, the quote pair, parameter prefix/suffix, the array and OpenAI wrappers and force handling. The rebase is a single insertion of 1256 lines with no canon line removed (canon already carried the PEG_SPACE/CHARS/STRING/SCHEMA/AC constants and all peg_dump_node branches; only the gate fixtures needed the new kind map). Gates against libllama-common: structural 13/13 (dump equality and rebuild identity, node counts identical to the earlier sub-566 run) and parse 9/9; mutations 15/15 in two halves plus 5/5 parse mutations. Exports 81+1 -> 83+1, nothing lost, no duplicates. The canonical runtime source is now EXP574 (17575 lines). 2026-11-14 EXP593 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-593-p7-08-parsers): nine model-output parser families are Goose - TranslateGemma, Functionary v3.2, GigaChat V3, Muse Glimmer, MiniCPM5, Harmony XML, Muse Spark, K2 Horizon and LLM-jp Harmony. The rebased draft had two real defects: Muse advanced its seven-byte <|eom|>/<|eot|> token by six, leaving a '>' that broke every exact prefix check (this produced the empty muse-glimmer reasoning, the dropped commentary tail and the missing muse-spark tool calls), and K2 Horizon XML did not emit the opening '{' and sliced arguments from the first parameter. Both are fixed; five Muse sites consume the full token and K2 emits call_start + d_params_begin and slices from the call start. Gate: 18 cases / 99 values / 0 failures against the native chat session over all nine families; mutations 12/12 in two halves. The canonical runtime source is now EXP593 (19025 lines). Recorded limits: the second to=self block is not concatenated (no case), one ATEM invoke per message, 16 KiB argument buffers. 2026-11-14 slice accounting: with EXP593 the eight planned slices are complete - lexer, parser, value model, JSON output, builtins/filters (piecewise through EXP506, 512-527, 522, 523 and 551), runtime (19025 lines), chat layer and the nine parser families. The requirement stays PARTIAL because two acceptance items remain: hoisted rule names still use a builder-local id (0/4 against native to_gbnf), and the chat apply entry point (llama-chat.cpp) with time injection is still native. 2026-11-14 EXP615 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-14-615-p7-08-json-escape): the runtime chat-JSON escaper was still the pre-EXP565 copy and wrote \xNN for control bytes below 0x20 (except 
//	) and for every byte at or above 0x7f - an escape no JSON reader accepts. It now follows nlohmann:  ,  , 
, , 	, \u00XX for the other control bytes and raw UTF-8 above 0x20, matching the value-model fix from EXP565. Gate: chat_content_json against nlohmann::json over 14 strings (empty, quotes, backslash, each short escape, 0x01/0x1f, UTF-8, emoji, mixed) with 0 failures; mutations 12/12 in two halves; the furniture gates stay green (tool builders 13/13 + parse 9/9, grammar 5/5 + 36/36 drafts). 2026-11-15 EXP625 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-625-p7-08-hoisted-names): the hoisted native rule names are closed. The port now allocates a Ref node for rule() exactly as the native builder does (peg_rule_ref/peg_rule_seal, PEG_REF kind), builds constructed args in the native operator order, skips empty seq/choice children like the native writer, resolves the effective kind for literals, and descends into the schema child under the tool-<i>-schema rule name. Gate: gbnf=ok 13/13 (was 1/13), cases=13 failures=0, parse_cases=9 failures=0; mutations 27/27 in four halves plus parse mutations 5/5. Identity holds per node: CT-1 81/81, CT-2 107/107, CT-3 1/1, CT-4 11/11, CT-5 155/155. tasks.title: Port JSON,schema,PEG and grammar conversion infrastructure
tasks.acceptance: JSON/schema/PEG/grammar parsing/rendering and validation owned by Goose; malformed/deep/large input tests and native golden compatibility.
tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P7-09-INVENTORY.md): every parsing surface named by the criterion is NATIVE -- llama-grammar.cpp.o in the candidate has 0 gg_function_ symbols (21 llama_grammar_* + 8 accept symbols in libllama), and json_schema_to_grammar (5 symbols) lives in libllama-common which has 0 Goose marks in the entire library. Therefore any behavioural parity here compares the same implementation with itself; the grammar-constrained case in EXP351 was exactly that and its README now says so explicitly instead of counting it as evidence. What the item requires is porting llama-grammar.cpp (PEG-style grammar with parser, stack machine, state cache) plus JSON-schema-to-GBNF, a project the size of the minja port; not started. Not tested: malformed/deep/large input differentials, which would be native-vs-native. 2026-11-13 FIRST SLICE (EXP472, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-472-p7-09-schema-shape): the JSON-schema-to-GBNF shaping decisions are Goose: repetition kind selection (empty/?/+/#/{min,max}/separator), the separator recursion (min-1, optional wrapper), the object required-then-optional split with one branch per optional property, additionalProperties as an extra branch, the empty-object form and the comma-prefix rule. Gate vs a native transcription: 369 cases / 1569 values / 0 failures, 300 random property sets; ASan+UBSan clean; 8/8 mutations. Still native: rule-text emission, pattern/format handling, $ref and the PEG grammar parser. P7-09 stays PARTIAL. 2026-11-13 SECOND SLICE (EXP473, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-473-p7-09-refs): the $ref and rule-name decisions are Goose: byte-level sanitization (maximal invalid run -> one '-'), the fragment split at the first '#', the ref name 'ref'+fragment, visit's reserved/empty rule-name policy (19 reserved names), the sub-name form, _add_rule collision suffixing (same rule text reuses the name, otherwise the first free decimal suffix) and the _resolve_ref condition (visit only when the rule is absent and the ref is not being resolved; a missing target records Unresolved $ref with empty rule text). Gate vs a std::regex/std::map transcription: 2255 cases / 3291 values / 0 failures over all 256 single bytes, the reserved set, 400 random refs and a 912-step insertion sequence; ASan+UBSan clean; 14/14 mutations. Still native: rule-text emission, pattern/format, the schema walk and the PEG parser. 2026-11-13 THIRD SLICE (EXP474, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-474-p7-09-pattern): the pattern and format conversion is Goose - _pattern_to_rule (anchored check, literals merged, escape table, classes, groups/?:, alternation, *+?, {n,m} via build_repetition, sub-rule interning with the native 1-based index, wrapping), _visit_pattern outcomes (unsupported -> string fallback, invalid -> reason and no rule), the dot rule for both dotall settings, string format selection (uuid/date/time/date-time/length/plain), the length rule and format_literal. Gate against the REAL native converter: the fixture links the prebuilt llama-common objects and calls build_grammar, capturing the warning channel; comparisons cover status, chosen rule name, exact rule body and invalid reasons over 73 fixed patterns x 5 seeded rule maps x dotall, 900 random patterns, both dot rules, the format table, 24 length rules and 564 format_literal inputs: 1941 cases / 4607 values / 0 failures; ASan+UBSan clean; 22/22 mutations. Still native: the schema walk and rule assembly for objects/tuples/arrays/integers, the built-in rule texts and the PEG parser. 2026-11-13 FOURTH SLICE (EXP475, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-475-p7-09-visit): the visit() rule-text assembly is Goose - object body (required kv chain, optional alternatives, recursive <name>-<key>-rest rules with same-name/text reuse, the '*' additional branch, the empty object), tuple, array (build_repetition with the ',' space separator and negative max -> unbounded), anyOf union, kv and additional-kv text, and the empty-object+ANY shortcut. tasks.acceptance: Goose entrypoint owns HTTP/API lifecycle; link/source/import audit shows no owned original C++ server/parser/task logic remains.
tasks.evidence: 2026-11-15 analysis (docs/goose-migration/P8-12-P4-13-ANALYSIS.md): the merged server sources exist (all four ports in one server-context.cpp, 29 references, 158 changed lines) and link_server.py relinks libllama-server-impl.so with the four bridges (rc=0, 19 defined / 0 undefined fg symbols). The shipped llama-server is not built from them yet, the S2.3 call sites (49 files / 18318 lines) are not switched, and the removal order must follow the switch order. Prerequisite: the M1 staged build that links llama-server with the server flags and does not run a model. 2026-11-15 EXP661 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-661-p8-12b-server-switches): the merged server sources build and link (OFF/ON 19 608 544 / 19 692 888 B phase A, 19 608 376 / 19 692 728 B phase B; step-1 baselines byte-identical). Two call sites are runtime switches with Goose as the default (rule 10): model status and Origin host. The native server_model_status_to_string body is removed; the OFF arm answers unknown, which the gate records. The gate passes 15/15 on ON (9 statuses + 3 localhost hosts + 3 refusals) and mutations 12/12 in halves. A previous-step defect was fixed: goose_init was never called, so fgs_init_early now runs at the start of llama_server plus a lazy start in the bridge. 2026-11-15 EXP663 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-15-663-p8-12c-mime-cache-tools): the remaining three sites are promoted and ON by default. Asset content type (mime-table.goose) and Cache-Control (web-assets.goose) lost their native bodies in the serve path; the built-in tool dispatch (tools-pure.goose tool_index) keeps its native linear scan because find_tool also serves MCP tools appended at run time, and the module index is trusted only when the native vector holds the same name at that position. OFF/ON 19 608 584 / 19 692 904 B, default configure 19 692 904 B with goose_init once; the differential gate is 150/150 in five runs (explicit init, lazy init, native arms, OFF stubs, default) and the mutations are 36/36 in three halves of twelve. Re-verified independently at acceptance. 2026-11-18 EXP995: two defects, both in my own accounting. (1) The adapter-debt figure was understated by two files: the enumeration was ls integration/goose-standalone/*.c, and cli/ is a subdirectory, so serve-main.c (133 lines) and tokenize-main.c (213) were never counted - not because they are tests but because the glob stopped a level short, while the comment claimed only tests/ is excluded. Now enumerated with find (8 files / 2192 lines, was 6 / 1818) and the report names how many files are excluded and why. The honest number is worse, which is the point: debt must not drift down because of an enumeration gap. (2) tools/check-adapter-parallelism.py turns the comment "an adapter is translation only" into a check - no adapter may define a function sharing a name with a Goose export - and found on_signal in serve-main.c defined while goose/server/shutdown-policy.goose exports it. The hit was real: the module owned the policy (first interrupt runs the shutdown, second forces exit(1) with a message) and was in NO composed unit, so nothing could reach it, while the host had its own any-signal-means-stop rule. Fixed: shutdown-policy.goose renamed its private helpers to sp_put/sp_st_i64 (its put/st_i64 conflicted with other modules, which is why it could not simply be added) and joined the unit (142 -> 143 modules); fg448_st_i64 added to the host as a three-word store and nothing else; serve-main.c keeps only an async-signal-safe counter and asks on_signal from the loop. signal-policy gate: 7 checks. Unit 1166 globals, 0 duplicates, 147 extern. Whole suite 38281 checks across 10 tests, 0 failures. Live server serves a request and exits cleanly on SIGTERM. shutdown_plan stays unwired: the standalone server has no sessions, models or backend to tear down in that order.

A synthetic unaligned layout (10/10/10 -> 96) was added after the unpadded-total mutation was missed on the real file. P9-02 stays IN_PROGRESS. 2026-11-13 SECOND SLICE (EXP458, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-458-p9-02-file-io): bounded reader decisions are Goose from gguf_reader: scalar fit, array limits (1<<30 elements, overflow guard, remaining bytes), string limits (1<<30, remaining bytes), seek bound and new remaining count, chunked transfer with file-end clamp and EOF zeroing the remaining count, and file_remain. Corrections: const declarations are module globals so the wrapper must run gg_init_globals; the overflow guard needed element sizes above 1<<33 and EOF coverage needed over-claimed remaining counts; two candidate mutations (chunk granulation, empty-tail file_remain) are unobservable and were dropped rather than counted; native seek takes uint64 so negative targets are rejected. NOT YET: mmap/pinned allocation, shard offsets, endian cases. P9-02 stays IN_PROGRESS. 2026-11-13 THIRD SLICE (EXP459, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-459-p9-02-shards): shard naming and validation are Goose from llama_split_path and the loader's n_split>1 block: "<prefix>-%05d-of-%05d.gguf" with split_no+1, %05d padding that widens instead of truncating, the snprintf capacity rule including the terminator, the first-shard/first-split rule, listed-count equality, per-file split.no equality, tensor-total equality, and the endian guard (only LE magic 0x46554747 and v2/v3; native gguf.cpp has no byte-swap path). Notes: the compiler shares identical bodies (count/index/tensor checks emit one function), and snprintf's terminator is part of the contract. NOT YET: mmap/pinned allocation. P9-02 stays IN_PROGRESS. 2026-11-13 FOURTH SLICE (EXP460, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-460-p9-02-mmap): mmap/direct-I/O/mlock decisions are Goose from llama-model-loader.cpp and llama-mmap.cpp: use_mmap for AUTO/MMAP/MMAP_MLOCK with the unsupported-platform fallback, use_direct_io for DIRECT_IO, use_mlock for MLOCK/MMAP_MLOCK, the data-offset alignment gate against the backend alignment, the direct-I/O staging plan (aligned start, offset in window, rounded byte count, 64 MiB buffer cap, skip), the 64MiB+2*alignment vs 1MiB staging buffer size, page-aligned mlock growth that stops after a failure, and page alignment of unmap ranges with the empty-range clamp. Gate vs native transcriptions: 1783 cases / 1983 values / 0 failures including a 200-read staging simulation compared byte-for-byte with the file window; ASan+UBSan clean; 10/10 mutations. System calls stay native. NOT YET: the async-upload staging ring and pinned host buffers. P9-02 stays IN_PROGRESS. 2026-11-13 FIFTH SLICE (EXP461, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-461-p9-02-upload-ring): async-upload ring decisions are Goose: max read alignment across files (floor 1), four-buffer rotation, the chunk plan (min(buffer,remaining), leading padding skipped on the first chunk, trailing padding trimmed on the last), the eligibility chain with one reason code per failing condition (mmap/checking, buffer, device, default buft, async/host/event caps, host buft, allocation/backend), and the biggest-first staged-tensor ordering. P9-02 stays IN_PROGRESS. 2026-11-13 SIXTH SLICE (EXP464, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-464-p9-02-read-path): mmap/pread read decisions are Goose from llama-mmap.cpp: buffered plan with EOF truncation and the short-read rule, errno action table (EINTR retry, EFAULT/EINVAL fallback, otherwise fatal), EOF zero-fill only at exactly the file size, read alignment (block size for O_DIRECT, 1 buffered), mapping-vs-file source selection and the mapping byte offset. work_front.note: Integrated stage-run (Apex): pinned at 4992 MiB cache, ctx 262144, reference argv. Decode ~40.4 @512 in this session's conditions; every accepted figure carries reference hash c2ff42cc1219. Nominal identical configs measured 39.6-41.8 across hours, so only paired same-session comparisons are used. The MoE expert-cache path is Goose throughout: admission (fg262a), copy run-lengths (fg263c), SLRU policy (fg756s). EXP-757 made the protected ceiling a parameter with a two-arm gate (provenance == native, and specification == chosen policy, both 100/100); measured hit rate 83.7 -> 84.8%, upload -6.7%. EXP-758: 384 MiB of cache outweighs that gain, so VRAM remains binding. Standalone: reads the full 21.7 GB payload (753 tensors, 0 mismatches); 20/20 harnesses pass at real dimensions; and the VALUE path now works - a real q4_K tensor dequantises and matmuls to 3.5e-03 of the f32 reference, q6_K to 2.9e-03, f32 exactly 0, with the Goose builder bit-identical to raw ggml (gb_vs_ggml=0) on all three types, and two real q4_K tensors CHAINED through the builder with the first node feeding the second (builder_vs_ggml=0, EXP: REAL-CHAIN-20261117). A SIX-node chain now runs on real weights and is bit-identical to raw ggml (builder_vs_ggml=0): rms_norm -> scale by the real blk.3.attn_norm.weight -> wq (q4_K, full 8192) -> qg_split -> CONT -> wo. That is everything an attention layer does before rope. Three rules learned the hard way, all from reading goose/model/qgate-split.goose rather than guessing: the q projection must carry its FULL 2*HD*H width; qg_split's output is 3-D and needs GGML_OP_CONT with explicit extents (mode 24, sizes in args 7..10); and qg_split's elem argument is the ELEMENT SIZE IN BYTES (4 for f32), not a mode - its head_stride is elem*HD*2 = 2048, and using the tensor row stride instead was wrong by 32x. Next: rope, the k/v path with softmax-weighted values, the MoE block, then the 41-layer loop. NOT done: the 41 layers are not composed into a pass (no residual carry, no embedding/output projection, no shared KV/state arena, no chunked prefill); no HTTP transport, no CUDA, no tokenizer engine. runtime/core (the target of 22 PARTIAL remainders) is built by nothing, so those remainders are unverifiable until it gets a build target or is retargeted at the standalone lineage. 2026-11-17 EXP920: a libc-only Goose tokenizer+detokenizer now matches libllama exactly on the Apex vocabulary (70 cases/11017 ids, 496640 pieces, 140 detokenize calls, eog set); the shipping server is still native, so P7-06/P7-07 are PARTIAL with their wire-up as the last slice. 2026-11-17 EXP922 (experiments/EXP-2026-11-17-922-goose-generation): the accepted Goose modules now run as one unit and generate real text on the Apex weights - Goose tokenizer -> Goose trunk (generic GGML CPU executor) -> Goose sampler -> Goose detokenizer -> stop on the Goose end-of-generation set. Greedy, same profile as the reference (Q4_0 KV, flash attention): 8 tokens and a 17-token chat run are id-identical and text-identical to native llama.cpp, including the '<|im_end|>' stop at step 16; a 32-token run produced continuous text. Two harness findings: default F32 KV/auto attention changes the continuation (profile, not a port defect), and a position-less batch re-reads the prompt on this hybrid model. The shipping server is still native; batch>1, GPU, the stochastic chain end to end and all speed figures remain unmeasured. 2026-11-17 EXP923 (open): the composed Goose runtime generates text with the same ids, text and EOS as llama.cpp on the tested greedy runs, but the logits are NOT equal (mean |d| 0.107 one token, 0.201 multi-token, 0 of 248320 bitwise). Native's own Q4_0-vs-F32 KV effect is smaller (0.077) than the Goose-vs-native gap, and Goose is not closer to native's Q4_0 run than to its F32 run, so this is a structural difference in the trunk graph, not KV quantisation alone. EXP918's bitwise gate compared against a hand-written native graph in the same fixture, which does not imply agreement with llama.cpp. The stochastic chain cannot be compared end to end until the logits agree; isolation by layer is the next slice. 2026-11-17 EXP923 closed its isolation work: every structural candidate in the trunk's attention branch was eliminated by ablation on truncated real-weight models (MoE/norms/residual/head bitwise equal; q/k, head norms, rope, gate split, wo not the cause; stored V canonical; view geometry right; kernel exact; permutation identical), and the residue is at the level of native's own quantisation spread (mean 0.1723 vs native Q4_0, while native's own Q4_0-vs-F32 spread is 0.1462, argmax identical everywhere). The acceptance-criterion question (a recorded tolerance band) is with Igor. The next unblocked area is model/OS ownership: the mapping is still borrowed from the caller, and the shipping path still owns nothing.

states.P7-06: The encode side now has an equal port: the standalone Goose tokenizer produces the same 114 ids as llama_tokenize on twenty-three prompts as one text (fenced code, a markdown table, emoji, mixed Japanese and English, two special tokens on a line, a URL, tabs, trailing spaces, accented Latin) and both with and without BOS - 227 ids identical in each - ASCII, Python, Cyrillic, Japanese, a long rare word, doubled spaces, a special-token marker, punctuation, numbers and a trailing newline (EXP-2026-11-19-1375). The decode side that shares this module is finished and served. Remainder: the runtime still takes the native encode decision, so step 2 of the plan - serving bt_bpe at llama_vocab::tokenize - is what remains, plus wider prompt coverage than ten cases. The encoder now runs at llama_tokenize in the shipped library under FG_TK_BPE_DIAG: the table builds in seconds through a new bulk door (gr_arr_str_offsets), the call has C linkage, and the GGUF check itself was made linear - it had been unusable on a real vocabulary. The comparison was also driven by a real server with chat templates - 73 live llama_tokenize calls, zero disagreements - and the library-side no-bos path is equal on the probe set, with the caveat that this vocabulary adds no BOS (EXP-2026-11-19-1393). Serving remains: the guard is in place and the evidence exists; the conversion and its acceptance triple are what is left. The encoder SERVES llama_tokenize behind FG_TK_BPE_SERVE and the pre-type guard: on a text prompt through the server both paths give the identical answer hash deb812577837a6f7 over 662 characters, with the served counter confirming the port answered. Covered gap: the acceptance request carries token ids, so its hash can never be evidence about the tokenizer - a text-prompt request has to join the acceptance profile for that (EXP-2026-11-19-1394). The gap is closed: with a text-prompt request of the same size (128 000 characters, about 32 000 tokens) the native and served encoders give the IDENTICAL answer hash 2d38a6fd6a03 with decode 63.7-64.4 in both, so the encoder is equal at acceptance scale and not only on probes (EXP-2026-11-19-1395). The encode path was swept over the WHOLE vocabulary: 248 320 token texts tokenised, zero disagreements, with the port serving every call (EXP-2026-11-19-1397). Two initial disagreements were an instrument error - the comparison stripped BOS/EOS without checking add_special - fixed and re-run to zero. Other pre-tokenizer families remain native by the guard, which is the remaining scope of this requirement. The model-name attribute overrides (phi-3, modern-bert, the <mask> rule) are NOT implemented in the port, and are verified not to apply to the family it serves: Apex is pre=qwen35, arch=qwen35moe, name=Apex-35B-V1.0, and none of the three native branches matches (EXP-2026-11-19-1413). The pre-type guard is what keeps that safe, and any family that needs an override must have its rule ported before it is served.
states.P7-07: The port serves every detokeniser decision on every path, including a short caller buffer: the door reports the same -needed the native does (EXP-1357) and its answer is served whichever sign it has (EXP-1358). The native call remains only as a guard for a door that cannot answer, which cannot be exercised while the library is linked against itself. Evidence: 21513 calls equal during measurement, 84 sequence calls over lengths, shapes and flags, a 32768-token equality case, and an unchanged acceptance hash at decode 63.10. The streaming boundaries were checked against non-streaming output: three requests, 26/49/49 fragments, byte-identical reassembly including a prompt that produces Japanese, so multi-byte fragmentation through the ported detokeniser is exercised (EXP-2026-11-19-1398). Not covered: truncation that ends mid-character and cancelled requests. The two open edge cases are measured: truncation in the middle of multi-byte text at n_predict 2/3/5 gives equal streamed and plain answers with no U+FFFD, and a stream cancelled after 179 fragments leaves the server serving the next request normally (EXP-2026-11-19-1399). Not covered: concurrent slots, cancel during prefill, and a client that never reads the body. The client-abandons case is measured too: a streaming request sent and the socket closed without reading a byte leaves the server answering 200 and alive (EXP-2026-11-19-1410). Remaining from that list: concurrent slots, which needs -np 2 and is therefore an exploration, and cancellation during prefill. Cancellation during prefill is measured as well: a 32K-token prompt abandoned after 0.8 s leaves the server answering 200 and alive (EXP-2026-11-19-1411). Of the three edges listed, only concurrent slots remains, and that needs -np 2, which is outside the accepted profile.
states.P7-12: GGUF and common native dependencies. The reader's closure is composed into the shipped unit (14 gr_* doors) and the port is proven against the native reader on the real 20 GB model file: five header fields; all 52 metadata keys by their own type (26 integers, 13 strings, 4 floats, 4 booleans, 5 arrays by element type and count); all 744231 array elements including the 248320-token vocabulary and the merge list; all 753 tensor names resolving to the same index; all 753 tensor descriptors (dtype, dims, extents, data offset); and an absent key reported absent by both (EXP-2026-11-19-1327). Gaps recorded: the reader exposes no accessor for tensor descriptors, so a host can find a tensor by name but cannot ask what it is; and nothing is connected - the loader still parses GGUF natively, so this is a proven port, not a finished one. The reader verification now covers the value classes it used to skip: float32 through gr_meta_f32_bits compared BIT FOR BIT (two NaNs or a signed zero would pass == and fail this), float64 narrowed to float32 as the accessor does, and booleans as 0/1. On Apex that is 34/34 values instead of 26/26 plus 744231 array elements, all equal (EXP-2026-11-19-1400). This matters because recurrent_layers is a bool array that decides which layers take the recurrent path.
